[Paleontology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paleontology "Paleontology") or palaeontology is the study of [prehistoric](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prehistory "Prehistory")[life forms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organism "Organism") on [Earth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earth "Earth") through the examination of plant and animal [fossils](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fossil "Fossil").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_in_paleontology#cite_note-1) This includes the study of body fossils, tracks ([ichnites](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ichnites "Ichnites")), [burrows](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burrow "Burrow"), cast-off parts, fossilised [feces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feces "Feces") ([coprolites](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coprolite "Coprolite")), [palynomorphs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palynomorph "Palynomorph") and [chemical residues](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Residue_(chemistry) "Residue (chemistry)"). Because humans have encountered fossils for millennia, paleontology has a long history both before and after becoming formalized as a [science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Science "Science"). This article records significant discoveries and events related to paleontology that occurred or were published in the year 2011.

[Paleontology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paleontology "Paleontology") or palaeontology is the study of [prehistoric](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prehistory "Prehistory")[life forms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organism "Organism") on [Earth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earth "Earth") through the examination of plant and animal [fossils](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fossil "Fossil").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_in_paleontology#cite_note-1) This includes the study of body fossils, tracks ([ichnites](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ichnites "Ichnites")), [burrows](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burrow "Burrow"), cast-off parts, fossilised [feces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feces "Feces") ([coprolites](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coprolite "Coprolite")), [palynomorphs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palynomorph "Palynomorph") and [chemical residues](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Residue_(chemistry) "Residue (chemistry)"). Because humans have encountered fossils for millennia, paleontology has a long history both before and after becoming formalized as a [science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Science "Science"). This article records significant discoveries and events related to paleontology that occurred or were published in the year 2011.

**Kansas** ([/ˈ k æ n z ə s/](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English")[](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/transcoded/e/e9/En-us-Kansas.ogg/En-us-Kansas.ogg.mp3 "Play audio")[ⓘ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:En-us-Kansas.ogg "File:En-us-Kansas.ogg")[_KAN-zəss_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key "Help:Pronunciation respelling key"))[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-11) is a landlocked [state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._state "U.S. state") in the [Midwestern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midwestern_United_States "Midwestern United States") region of the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-12) It borders [Nebraska](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nebraska "Nebraska") to the north, [Colorado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado "Colorado") to the west, [Oklahoma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oklahoma "Oklahoma") to the south, and [Missouri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri "Missouri") to the east. Kansas is named after the [Kansas River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_River "Kansas River"), in turn named after the [Kansa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaw_people "Kaw people") people.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-13)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-14)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-15)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-16) Its [capital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_capitals_in_the_United_States "List of capitals in the United States") is [Topeka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Topeka,_Kansas "Topeka, Kansas"), and its [most populous city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cities_in_Kansas "List of cities in Kansas") is [Wichita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wichita,_Kansas "Wichita, Kansas"); however, the largest urban area is the bi-state [Kansas City metropolitan area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City_metropolitan_area "Kansas City metropolitan area") surrounding [Kansas City, Missouri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City,_Missouri "Kansas City, Missouri"), which straddles the border of Kansas and Missouri.

For thousands of years, what is now known as Kansas was home to numerous and diverse [Indigenous tribes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plains_Indians "Plains Indians"). The first settlement of non-indigenous people in Kansas occurred in 1827 at [Fort Leavenworth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Leavenworth "Fort Leavenworth"). The pace of settlement accelerated in the 1850s, in the midst of political wars over the [slavery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slavery_in_the_United_States "Slavery in the United States") debate. When it was officially opened to settlement by the U.S. government in 1854 with the [Kansas–Nebraska Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas%E2%80%93Nebraska_Act "Kansas–Nebraska Act"), conflict between abolitionist [Free-Staters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free-Stater_(Kansas) "Free-Stater (Kansas)") from [New England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_England "New England") and pro-slavery settlers from neighboring Missouri broke out over the question of whether Kansas would become a [free state or a slave state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slave_states_and_free_states "Slave states and free states"), in a period known as [Bleeding Kansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bleeding_Kansas "Bleeding Kansas"). On January 29, 1861,[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-17)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-18) Kansas entered the [Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Union_(American_Civil_War) "Union (American Civil War)") as a free state, hence the unofficial nickname "The Free State". Passage of the [Homestead Acts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homestead_Acts "Homestead Acts") in 1862 brought a further influx of settlers, and the booming cattle trade of the 1870s attracted some of the Wild West's most iconic figures to western Kansas.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-19)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-20)

As of 2015, Kansas was among the most productive agricultural states, producing high yields of wheat, corn, [sorghum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sorghum "Sorghum"), and [soybeans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soybean "Soybean").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-21) In addition to its traditional strength in agriculture, Kansas possesses an extensive aerospace industry. Kansas, which has an area of 82,278 square miles (213,100 square kilometers) is the [15th-largest state by area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_U.S._states_and_territories_by_area "List of U.S. states and territories by area"), the [36th most-populous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_U.S._states_and_territories_by_population "List of U.S. states and territories by population") of the 50 states, with a population of 2,940,865[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-22) according to the 2020 census, and the [10th least densely populated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_states_and_territories_of_the_United_States_by_population_density "List of states and territories of the United States by population density"). Residents of Kansas are called _Kansans_ or _Jayhawkers_.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-23)[Mount Sunflower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Sunflower "Mount Sunflower") is Kansas's highest point at 4,039 feet (1,231 meters).[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-24)

Kansas is generally considered to be the geographic center of the [contiguous United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contiguous_United_States "Contiguous United States"), with [Lebanon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebanon,_Kansas "Lebanon, Kansas") being [approximately the center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geographic_center_of_the_contiguous_United_States "Geographic center of the contiguous United States").

## Etymology

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kansas&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Etymology")]

![Image 10: Exclamation mark with arrows pointing at each other](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2e/Ambox_contradict.svg/40px-Ambox_contradict.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)This section **appears to contradict itself**. Please see the [talk page](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talk:Kansas# "Talk:Kansas") for more information._(July 2026)_

The name _Kansas_ derives from the [Algonquian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algonquian_languages "Algonquian languages") term _Akansa_, referring to the [Quapaw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quapaw "Quapaw") people. These were a [Dhegiha Siouan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dhegiha_Siouan "Dhegiha Siouan")-speaking people who settled in [Arkansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arkansas "Arkansas") around the 13th century. The stem -_kansa_ is named after the [Kaw people](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaw_people "Kaw people"), also known as the _Kansa_, a federally recognized Native American tribe.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-25) The [tribe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_federally_recognized_tribes "List of federally recognized tribes")'s name (natively _\_kką:ze\__) is often said to mean "people of the (south) wind", although this was probably not the term's original meaning.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-26)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-27)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kansas&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: History")]

Main article: [History of Kansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Kansas "History of Kansas")

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/81/War_dance_in_the_interiour_of_a_Konza_lodge.jpg/250px-War_dance_in_the_interiour_of_a_Konza_lodge.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:War_dance_in_the_interiour_of_a_Konza_lodge.jpg)

Samuel Seymour's 1819 illustration of a [Kansa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaw_people "Kaw people") lodge and dance is the oldest drawing known to have been done in Kansas.

Before [European colonization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_colonization_of_the_Americas "European colonization of the Americas"), Kansas was occupied by the [Caddoan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caddoan "Caddoan")[Wichita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wichita_people "Wichita people") and later the [Siouan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siouan "Siouan")[Kaw people](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaw_people "Kaw people"). The Indigenous people in the eastern part of the state generally lived in villages along the river valleys. Those in the western part of the state were semi-nomadic and hunted large herds of [bison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bison "Bison").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] The first European to set foot in present-day Kansas was the Spanish [conquistador](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conquistador "Conquistador")[Francisco Vázquez de Coronado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francisco_V%C3%A1zquez_de_Coronado "Francisco Vázquez de Coronado"), who explored the area in 1541.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Between 1763 and 1803, the territory of Kansas was integrated into [Spanish Louisiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Louisiana "Spanish Louisiana"). During that period, Governor [Luis de Unzaga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_de_Unzaga "Luis de Unzaga") 'le Conciliateur' promoted expeditions and good relations with the [Amerindians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amerindians "Amerindians"). Explorer Antoine de Marigny and others continued trading across the [Kansas River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_River "Kansas River"), especially at its confluence with the [Missouri River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri_River "Missouri River"), tributaries of the [Mississippi River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mississippi_River "Mississippi River").[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-28)

In 1803, most of modern Kansas was [acquired by the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_territorial_acquisitions "United States territorial acquisitions") as part of the [Louisiana Purchase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisiana_Purchase "Louisiana Purchase"). Southwest Kansas, however, was still a part of Spain, Mexico, and the [Republic of Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_of_Texas "Republic of Texas") until the conclusion of the [Mexican–American War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexican%E2%80%93American_War "Mexican–American War") in 1848, when these lands were [ceded to the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexican_Cession "Mexican Cession"). From 1812 to 1821, Kansas was part of the [Missouri Territory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri_Territory "Missouri Territory"). The [Santa Fe Trail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Fe_Trail "Santa Fe Trail") traversed Kansas from 1821 to 1880, transporting manufactured goods from [Missouri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri "Missouri") and silver and furs from [Santa Fe, New Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Fe,_New_Mexico "Santa Fe, New Mexico"). [Wagon ruts from the trail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Fe_Trail_Remains "Santa Fe Trail Remains") are still visible in the prairie today.

In 1827, [Fort Leavenworth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Leavenworth "Fort Leavenworth") became the first permanent settlement of white Americans in the future state.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-29) The [Kansas–Nebraska Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas%E2%80%93Nebraska_Act "Kansas–Nebraska Act") became law on May 30, 1854, establishing [Nebraska Territory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nebraska_Territory "Nebraska Territory") and [Kansas Territory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_Territory "Kansas Territory"), and opening the area to broader settlement by whites. [Kansas Territory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_Territory "Kansas Territory") stretched all the way to the Continental Divide and included the sites of present-day [Denver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denver "Denver"), [Colorado Springs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs,_Colorado "Colorado Springs, Colorado"), and [Pueblo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pueblo,_Colorado "Pueblo, Colorado").

[![Image 12](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9b/Battle_of_Lawrence.png/250px-Battle_of_Lawrence.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Battle_of_Lawrence.png)

[Quantrill's Raid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawrence_Massacre "Lawrence Massacre") on [Lawrence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawrence,_Kansas "Lawrence, Kansas")

### Bleeding Kansas and the Civil War

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kansas&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Bleeding Kansas and the Civil War")]

The first non-military settlement of Euro-Americans in Kansas Territory consisted of [abolitionists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abolitionism_in_the_United_States "Abolitionism in the United States") from [Massachusetts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massachusetts "Massachusetts") and other [Free-Staters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free-Stater_(Kansas) "Free-Stater (Kansas)") who founded the town of Lawrence and attempted to stop the spread of slavery from neighboring Missouri.

Missouri and [Arkansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arkansas "Arkansas") continually sent settlers into Kansas Territory along its eastern border to sway votes in favor of slavery prior to Kansas statehood elections. Directly presaging the [American Civil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Civil_War "American Civil War") these forces collided, entering into skirmishes and guerrilla conflicts that earned the territory the nickname [Bleeding Kansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bleeding_Kansas "Bleeding Kansas"). These included [John Brown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Brown_(abolitionist) "John Brown (abolitionist)")'s [Pottawatomie massacre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pottawatomie_massacre "Pottawatomie massacre") of 1856.

Kansas was [admitted to the Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Admission_to_the_Union "Admission to the Union") as a free state on January 29, 1861, making it the 34th state to join the United States. By that time, the violence in Kansas had largely subsided, but during the Civil War, on August 21, 1863, [William Quantrill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Quantrill "William Quantrill") led several hundred of his supporters on a raid into [Lawrence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawrence,_Kansas "Lawrence, Kansas"), destroying much of the city and killing nearly 200 people. He was roundly condemned by both the conventional [Confederate military](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Confederate_States_Army "Confederate States Army") and the partisan rangers commissioned by the [Missouri legislature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri_legislature "Missouri legislature"). His application to that body for a commission was flatly rejected due to his pre-war criminal record.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-30)

### Settlement and the Wild West

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kansas&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Settlement and the Wild West")]

Passage of the [Homestead Acts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homestead_Acts "Homestead Acts") in 1862 accelerated settlement and agricultural development in the state. After the Civil War, many veterans constructed homesteads in Kansas. Many African Americans also looked to Kansas as the land of "[John Brown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Brown_(abolitionist) "John Brown (abolitionist)")" and, led by [freedmen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freedmen "Freedmen") like [Benjamin "Pap" Singleton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benjamin_%22Pap%22_Singleton "Benjamin \"Pap\" Singleton"), began establishing black colonies in the state. Leaving southern states in the late 1870s because of increasing discrimination, they became known as [Exodusters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exodusters "Exodusters").

At the same time, the [Chisholm Trail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chisholm_Trail "Chisholm Trail") was opened and the [Wild West](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Old_West "American Old West") era commenced in Kansas. Storied lawman [Wild Bill Hickok](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wild_Bill_Hickok "Wild Bill Hickok") was a deputy marshal at [Fort Riley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Riley "Fort Riley") and a marshal at [Hays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hays,_Kansas "Hays, Kansas") and [Abilene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abilene,_Kansas "Abilene, Kansas"). [Dodge City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dodge_City,_Kansas "Dodge City, Kansas") was home to both [Bat Masterson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bat_Masterson "Bat Masterson") and [Wyatt Earp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyatt_Earp "Wyatt Earp"), who worked as lawmen in the town. The [Dalton Gang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalton_Gang "Dalton Gang") robbed trains and banks throughout Kansas and the Southwest and maintained a hideout in [Meade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meade,_Kansas "Meade, Kansas"). During its 19th-century peak, Dodge City shipped up to 500,000 Texas cattle annually, cementing its reputation as the "Queen of the Cowtowns".

### 20th century

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kansas&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 20th century")]

In response to demands of [Methodists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Methodists "Methodists") and other [evangelical Protestants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evangelical_Protestants "Evangelical Protestants"), in 1881 Kansas became the first U.S. state to adopt a constitutional amendment [prohibiting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prohibition "Prohibition") all [alcoholic beverages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alcohol_laws_of_Kansas "Alcohol laws of Kansas"), which was repealed in 1948. Anti-saloon activist [Carrie Nation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carrie_Nation "Carrie Nation") vandalized her first saloon in [Kiowa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiowa,_Kansas "Kiowa, Kansas") in 1900. In 1922, suffragist [Ella Uphay Mowry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ella_Uphay_Mowry "Ella Uphay Mowry") became the first female gubernatorial candidate in the state when she ran as "Mrs. W.D. Mowry". She later stated: "Someone had to be the pioneer. I firmly believe that some day a woman will sit in the governor's chair in Kansas."[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-31)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-32)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-33)

Kansas suffered severe environmental damage in the 1930s due to the combined effects of the [Great Depression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Depression "Great Depression") and the [Dust Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dust_Bowl "Dust Bowl"), and large numbers of people left southwestern Kansas in particular for better opportunities elsewhere.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-34) The outbreak of [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II") spurred rapid growth in aircraft manufacturing near Wichita in the so-called [Battle of Kansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Kansas "Battle of Kansas"), and the aerospace sector remains a significant portion of the Kansan economy to this day.

Kansas is bordered by [Nebraska](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nebraska "Nebraska") to the north; [Missouri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri "Missouri") to the east; [Oklahoma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oklahoma "Oklahoma") to the south; and [Colorado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado "Colorado") to the west. The state is divided into [105 counties](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_counties_in_Kansas "List of counties in Kansas") with [628 cities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cities_in_Kansas "List of cities in Kansas"), with its largest county by area being [Butler County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Butler_County,_Kansas "Butler County, Kansas").[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-35) Kansas is located [equidistant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equidistant "Equidistant") from the Pacific and Atlantic oceans. The [geographic center of the 48 contiguous states](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geographic_center_of_the_contiguous_United_States "Geographic center of the contiguous United States") is in [Smith County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smith_County,_Kansas "Smith County, Kansas") near [Lebanon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebanon,_Kansas "Lebanon, Kansas"). Until 1989, the [Meades Ranch Triangulation Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meades_Ranch_Triangulation_Station "Meades Ranch Triangulation Station") in [Osborne County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Osborne_County,_Kansas "Osborne County, Kansas") was the geodetic center of North America: the central reference point for all maps of North America. The geographic center of Kansas is in [Barton County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barton_County,_Kansas "Barton County, Kansas").

### Geology

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kansas&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Geology")]

Main article: [Geology of Kansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geology_of_Kansas "Geology of Kansas")

Kansas is underlain by a sequence of horizontal to gently westward [dipping](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strike_and_dip "Strike and dip")[sedimentary rocks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedimentary_rock "Sedimentary rock"). A sequence of [Mississippian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mississippian_age "Mississippian age"), [Pennsylvanian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pennsylvanian_(geology) "Pennsylvanian (geology)") and [Permian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Permian "Permian") rocks outcrop in the eastern and southern part of the state. The state's western half has exposures of [Cretaceous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cretaceous "Cretaceous") through Tertiary sediments, the latter derived from the [erosion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erosion "Erosion") of the [uplifted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tectonic_uplift "Tectonic uplift")[Rocky Mountains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocky_Mountains "Rocky Mountains") to the west. These are underlain by older Paleozoic and Mesozoic sediments which correlate well with the outcrops to the east. The state's northeastern corner was subjected to [glaciation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glaciation "Glaciation") in the [Pleistocene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pleistocene "Pleistocene") and is covered by [glacial drift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glacial_drift "Glacial drift") and [loess](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loess "Loess").

### Topography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kansas&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Topography")]

The western third of the state, lying in the [great central plain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Plains "Great Plains") of the United States, has a generally flat or undulating surface, while the eastern third has many hills and forests; the middle third is generally hilly, with more sparse vegetation than the eastern third.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-36) The land gradually rises from east to west. Its altitude ranges from 684 ft (208 m) along the [Verdigris River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Verdigris_River "Verdigris River") at [Coffeyville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coffeyville,_Kansas "Coffeyville, Kansas") in [Montgomery County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montgomery_County,_Kansas "Montgomery County, Kansas"), to 4,039 ft (1,231 m) at [Mount Sunflower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Sunflower "Mount Sunflower"), 0.5 miles (0.80 kilometers) from the Colorado border, in [Wallace County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wallace_County,_Kansas "Wallace County, Kansas"). It is a common misconception that Kansas is the flattest state in the nation—in 2003, a tongue-in-cheek study famously declared the state "flatter than a pancake".[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-37) Kansas has a maximum topographic relief of 3,360 ft (1,020 m),[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-38) making it the 23rd flattest U.S. state measured by maximum relief.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-39)

### Rivers

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kansas&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Rivers")]

See also: [List of rivers of Kansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_rivers_of_Kansas "List of rivers of Kansas")

[![Image 16](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/32/Spring_River_2006-07-03_2104.jpg/250px-Spring_River_2006-07-03_2104.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Spring_River_2006-07-03_2104.jpg)

[Spring River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spring_River_(Missouri) "Spring River (Missouri)"), Kansas

Around 74 mi (119 km) of the state's northeastern boundary is defined by the [Missouri River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri_River "Missouri River"). The [Kansas River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_River "Kansas River") (locally known as the Kaw), formed by the junction of the [Smoky Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smoky_Hill_River "Smoky Hill River") and [Republican](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_River "Republican River") rivers at appropriately named [Junction City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Junction_City,_Kansas "Junction City, Kansas"), joins the Missouri River at [Kansas City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City,_Kansas "Kansas City, Kansas"), after a course of 170 mi (270 km) across the northeastern part of the state.

The [Arkansas River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arkansas_River "Arkansas River") ([pronunciation varies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arkansas_River#Pronunciations "Arkansas River")), rising in [Colorado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado "Colorado"), flows with a bending course for nearly 500 mi (800 km) across the western and southern parts of the state. With its tributaries, (the [Little Arkansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Little_Arkansas_River "Little Arkansas River"), [Ninnescah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ninnescah_River "Ninnescah River"), Walnut, [Cow Creek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cow_Creek_(Kansas) "Cow Creek (Kansas)"), [Cimarron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cimarron_River_(Arkansas_River) "Cimarron River (Arkansas River)"), Verdigris, and the [Neosho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neosho_River "Neosho River")), it forms the southern drainage system of the state.

Kansas's other rivers are the [Saline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saline_River_(Kansas) "Saline River (Kansas)") and Solomon Rivers, tributaries of the Smoky Hill River; the [Big Blue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Blue_River_(Kansas) "Big Blue River (Kansas)"), [Delaware](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delaware_River_(Kansas) "Delaware River (Kansas)"), and [Wakarusa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wakarusa_River "Wakarusa River"), which flow into the Kansas River; and the [Marais des Cygnes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marais_des_Cygnes_River "Marais des Cygnes River"), a tributary of the Missouri River. Spring River is located between [Riverton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverton,_Kansas "Riverton, Kansas") and [Baxter Springs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baxter_Springs,_Kansas "Baxter Springs, Kansas").

In the [Köppen climate classification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K%C3%B6ppen_climate_classification "Köppen climate classification"), Kansas has three climates: humid continental, semi-arid steppe, and humid subtropical. The eastern two-thirds of the state (especially the northeastern portion) has a [humid continental climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humid_continental_climate "Humid continental climate"), with cool to cold winters and hot, often humid summers. Most of the precipitation falls during both the summer and the spring. The [USDA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USDA "USDA")[hardiness zones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hardiness_zone "Hardiness zone") for Kansas range from Zone 5b (−15°F to −10°F) in the North to Zone 7a (0°F to 5°F) in the South.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-46)

The western third of the state—from roughly the [U.S. Route 83](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Route_83 "U.S. Route 83") corridor westward—has a [semi-arid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semi-arid_climate "Semi-arid climate")[steppe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steppe "Steppe") climate. Summers are hot, often very hot, and generally less humid. Winters are highly changeable between warm and very cold. The western region receives an average of about 16 inches (410 millimeters) of precipitation per year. [Chinook winds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinook_wind "Chinook wind") in the winter can warm western Kansas all the way into the 80 degrees Fahrenheit (27 degrees Celsius) range.

The south-central and southeastern portions of the state, including the [Wichita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wichita,_Kansas "Wichita, Kansas") area, have a [humid subtropical climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humid_subtropical_climate "Humid subtropical climate") with hot and humid summers, milder winters, and more precipitation than elsewhere in Kansas. Some features of all three climates can be found in most of the state, with droughts and changeable weather between dry and humid not uncommon, and both warm and cold spells in the winter.

Temperatures in areas between U.S. Routes 83 and [81](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Route_81 "U.S. Route 81"), as well as the southwestern portion of the state along and south of [U.S. 50](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Route_50 "U.S. Route 50"), reach 90°F (32°C) or above on most days of June, July, and August. High humidity added to the high temperatures sends the [heat index](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heat_index "Heat index") into life-threatening territory, especially in Wichita, [Hutchinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hutchinson,_Kansas "Hutchinson, Kansas"), [Salina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salina,_Kansas "Salina, Kansas"), [Russell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russell,_Kansas "Russell, Kansas"), [Hays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hays,_Kansas "Hays, Kansas"), and [Great Bend](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Bend,_Kansas "Great Bend, Kansas"). Temperatures are often higher in [Dodge City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dodge_City,_Kansas "Dodge City, Kansas"), [Garden City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garden_City,_Kansas "Garden City, Kansas"), and [Liberal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberal,_Kansas "Liberal, Kansas"), but the heat index in those three cities is usually lower than the actual air temperature.

Although temperatures of 100°F (38°C) or higher are not as common in areas east of U.S. 81, higher humidity and the [urban heat island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urban_heat_island "Urban heat island") effect lead most summer days to heat indices between 107 and 114°F (42 and 46°C) in [Topeka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Topeka,_Kansas "Topeka, Kansas"), [Lawrence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawrence,_Kansas "Lawrence, Kansas"), and the [Kansas City metropolitan area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City_metropolitan_area "Kansas City metropolitan area"). Also, combined with humidity between 85 and 95 percent, dangerous heat indices can be experienced at every hour of the day.

Precipitation ranges from about 47 inches (1,200 mm) annually in the state's southeast corner to about 16 inches (410 mm) in the southwest. Snowfall ranges from around 5 inches (130 mm) in the fringes of the south, to 35 inches (890 mm) in the far northwest. Frost-free days range from more than 200 days in the south, to 130 days in the northwest. Thus, Kansas is the country's ninth or tenth sunniest state, depending on the source. Western Kansas is as sunny as parts of California and [Arizona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arizona "Arizona").

Kansas is prone to severe weather, especially in the spring and the early-summer. Despite the frequent sunshine throughout much of the state, due to its location at a climatic boundary prone to intrusions of multiple air masses, the state is vulnerable to strong and severe thunderstorms. Some of these storms become [supercell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supercell "Supercell") thunderstorms; these can produce some [tornadoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tornado "Tornado"), occasionally those of [EF3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enhanced_Fujita_scale "Enhanced Fujita scale") strength or higher. Kansas averages more than 50 tornadoes annually.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-Annual_Average_Number_of_Tornadoes-47) Severe thunderstorms sometimes drop some very large [hail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hail "Hail") over Kansas as well. Furthermore, these storms can even bring in flash flooding and damaging straight line winds.

According to NOAA, the all-time highest temperature recorded in Kansas is (121°F or 49.4°C) on July 24, 1936, near [Alton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alton,_Kansas "Alton, Kansas") in [Osborne County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Osborne_County,_Kansas "Osborne County, Kansas"), and the all-time low is −40°F (−40°C) on February 13, 1905, near [Lebanon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebanon,_Kansas "Lebanon, Kansas") in [Smith County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smith_County,_Kansas "Smith County, Kansas"). Alton and Lebanon are approximately 50 miles (80 km) apart.

Kansas's record high of 121°F (49.4°C) ties with [North Dakota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Dakota "North Dakota") for the fifth-highest record high in an American state, behind California (134°F or 56.7°C), [Arizona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arizona "Arizona") (128°F or 53.3°C), [Nevada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nevada "Nevada") (125°F or 51.7°C), and [New Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico "New Mexico") (122°F or 50°C).

Kansas has 627 [incorporated cities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Municipal_corporation "Municipal corporation"). By state statute, cities are divided into three classes as determined by the population obtained "by any census of enumeration". A city of the third class has a population of less than 5,000, but cities reaching a population of more than 2,000 may be certified as a city of the second class. The second class is limited to cities with a population of less than 25,000, and upon reaching a population of more than 15,000, they may be certified as a city of the first class. First and second class cities are independent of any [township](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_township "Civil township") and are not included within the township's territory.

### Life expectancy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kansas&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Life expectancy")]

The residents of Kansas have a life expectancy near the U.S. national average. In 2013, males in Kansas lived an average of 76.6 years compared to a male national average of 76.7 years and females lived an average of 81.0 years compared to a female national average of 81.5 years. Increases in life expectancy between 1980 and 2013 were below the national average for males and near the national average for females. Male life expectancy in Kansas between 1980 and 2014 increased by an average of 5.2 years, compared to a male national average of a 6.7-year increase. Life expectancy for females in Kansas between 1980 and 2014 increased by 4.3 years, compared to a female national average of a 4.0 year increase.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-61)

Using 2017–2019 data, the [Robert Wood Johnson Foundation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Wood_Johnson_Foundation "Robert Wood Johnson Foundation") calculated that life expectancy for Kansas counties ranged from 75.8 years for [Wyandotte County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyandotte_County,_Kansas "Wyandotte County, Kansas") to 81.7 years for [Johnson County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnson_County,_Kansas "Johnson County, Kansas"). Life expectancy for the state as a whole was 78.5 years.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-Robert_Wood_Johnson-62) Life expectancy for the United States as a whole in 2019 was 78.8 years.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-Mortality-63)

### Regions

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kansas&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Regions")]

#### Northeast Kansas

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kansas&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Northeast Kansas")]

[![Image 22](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/69/UK_Strong_Hall_Lawrence_Nima_02.jpg/250px-UK_Strong_Hall_Lawrence_Nima_02.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:UK_Strong_Hall_Lawrence_Nima_02.jpg)

[University of Kansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Kansas "University of Kansas") Strong Hall in Lawrence

The northeastern portion of the state, extending from the eastern border to [Junction City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Junction_City,_Kansas "Junction City, Kansas") and from the Nebraska border to south of Johnson County is home to more than 1.5 million people in the Kansas City (Kansas portion), Manhattan, Lawrence, and Topeka [metropolitan areas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_area "Metropolitan area"). [Overland Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overland_Park,_Kansas "Overland Park, Kansas"), a young city incorporated in 1960, has the largest population and the largest land area in the county. It is home to [Johnson County Community College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnson_County_Community_College "Johnson County Community College").

Olathe is the [county seat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_seat "County seat") and home to [Johnson County Executive Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnson_County_Executive_Airport "Johnson County Executive Airport"). The cities of Olathe, [Shawnee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawnee,_Kansas "Shawnee, Kansas"), [De Soto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/De_Soto,_Kansas "De Soto, Kansas") and [Gardner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gardner,_Kansas "Gardner, Kansas") have some of the state's fastest growing populations. The cities of Overland Park, [Lenexa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lenexa,_Kansas "Lenexa, Kansas"), Olathe, De Soto, and Gardner are also notable because they lie along the former route of the [Santa Fe Trail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Fe_Trail "Santa Fe Trail"). Among cities with at least one thousand residents, [Mission Hills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mission_Hills,_Kansas "Mission Hills, Kansas") has the highest median income in the state.

Several institutions of higher education are located in Northeast Kansas including [Baker University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baker_University "Baker University") (the oldest university in the state, founded in 1858 and affiliated with the [United Methodist Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Methodist_Church "United Methodist Church")) in Baldwin City, [Benedictine College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benedictine_College "Benedictine College") (sponsored by [St. Benedict's Abbey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Benedict's_Abbey "St. Benedict's Abbey") and [Mount St. Scholastica Monastery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benedictine_Sisters_of_Mount_St._Scholastica "Benedictine Sisters of Mount St. Scholastica") and formed from the merger of St. Benedict's College (1858) and Mount St. Scholastica College (1923)) in Atchison, [MidAmerica Nazarene University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MidAmerica_Nazarene_University "MidAmerica Nazarene University") in Olathe, [Ottawa University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ottawa_University "Ottawa University") in Ottawa and Overland Park, Kansas City Kansas Community College and KU Medical Center in Kansas City, and KU Edwards Campus in Overland Park. Less than an hour's drive to the west, [Lawrence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawrence,_Kansas "Lawrence, Kansas") is home to the [University of Kansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Kansas "University of Kansas"), the largest public university in the state, and [Haskell Indian Nations University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haskell_Indian_Nations_University "Haskell Indian Nations University").

To the north, [Kansas City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City,_Kansas "Kansas City, Kansas"), with the second-largest land area in the state, contains a number of diverse ethnic neighborhoods. Its attractions include the [Kansas Speedway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_Speedway "Kansas Speedway"), [Sporting Kansas City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sporting_Kansas_City "Sporting Kansas City"), [Kansas City Monarchs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City_Monarchs_(American_Association) "Kansas City Monarchs (American Association)"), and [The Legends at Village West](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legends_at_Village_West "The Legends at Village West") retail and entertainment center. Nearby, Kansas's first settlement [Bonner Springs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bonner_Springs,_Kansas "Bonner Springs, Kansas")[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-autogenerated1-64) is home to several national and regional attractions including the [Providence Medical Center Amphitheater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cricket_Wireless_Amphitheater_(Bonner_Springs,_Kansas) "Cricket Wireless Amphitheater (Bonner Springs, Kansas)"), the [National Agricultural Center and Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Agricultural_Center_and_Hall_of_Fame "National Agricultural Center and Hall of Fame"), and the annual [Kansas City Renaissance Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City_Renaissance_Festival "Kansas City Renaissance Festival"). Further up the [Missouri River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri_River "Missouri River"), the city of [Lansing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lansing,_Kansas "Lansing, Kansas") is the home of the state's first maximum-security prison. Historic [Leavenworth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leavenworth,_Kansas "Leavenworth, Kansas"), founded in 1854, was the first incorporated city in Kansas. North of the city, [Fort Leavenworth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Leavenworth "Fort Leavenworth") is the oldest active Army post west of the [Mississippi River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mississippi_River "Mississippi River"). The city of [Atchison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atchison,_Kansas "Atchison, Kansas") was an early commercial center in the state and is well known as the birthplace of [Amelia Earhart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amelia_Earhart "Amelia Earhart").

[![Image 23](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/08/Kansas_State_Capitol_in_summer_2024.jpg/250px-Kansas_State_Capitol_in_summer_2024.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kansas_State_Capitol_in_summer_2024.jpg)

The [Kansas Statehouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_Statehouse "Kansas Statehouse")

To the west, nearly a quarter million people reside in the Topeka metropolitan area. [Topeka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Topeka,_Kansas "Topeka, Kansas") is the state capital and home to [Washburn University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washburn_University "Washburn University") and [Washburn Institute of Technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washburn_Institute_of_Technology "Washburn Institute of Technology"). Built at a [Kansas River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_River "Kansas River") crossing along the old [Oregon Trail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oregon_Trail "Oregon Trail"), this historic city has several nationally registered historic places. Further westward along [Interstate 70](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_70_(Kansas) "Interstate 70 (Kansas)") and the Kansas River is [Junction City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Junction_City,_Kansas "Junction City, Kansas") with its historic limestone and brick buildings and nearby [Fort Riley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Riley "Fort Riley"), well known as the home to the [U.S. Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Army "United States Army")'s [1st Infantry Division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1st_Infantry_Division_(United_States) "1st Infantry Division (United States)") (nicknamed "the Big Red One"). A short distance away, the city of [Manhattan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manhattan,_Kansas "Manhattan, Kansas") is home to [Kansas State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_State_University "Kansas State University"), the second-largest public university in the state and the nation's oldest land-grant university, dating back to 1863. South of the campus, [Aggieville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aggieville "Aggieville") dates back to 1889 and is the state's oldest shopping district of its kind.

#### South Central Kansas

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kansas&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: South Central Kansas")]

[![Image 24](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1f/Wichita%2C_Kansas_skyline_aerial_view.jpg/250px-Wichita%2C_Kansas_skyline_aerial_view.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Wichita,_Kansas_skyline_aerial_view.jpg)

Downtown Wichita in the winter

In south-central Kansas, the [Wichita metropolitan area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wichita_metropolitan_area,_Kansas "Wichita metropolitan area, Kansas") is home to more than 600,000 people.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-65)[Wichita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wichita,_Kansas "Wichita, Kansas") is the largest city in the state in terms of both land area and population. 'The Air Capital' is a major manufacturing center for the aircraft industry and the home of [Wichita State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wichita_State_University "Wichita State University"). Before Wichita was 'The Air Capital' it was a Cowtown.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-gowichita1-66) With a number of nationally registered historic places, museums, and other entertainment destinations, it has a desire to become a cultural mecca in the Midwest. Wichita's population growth has grown by double digits and the surrounding suburbs are among the fastest growing cities in the state. The population of [Goddard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goddard,_Kansas "Goddard, Kansas") has grown by more than 11% per year since 2000.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-2006SubEst-67) Other fast-growing cities include [Andover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andover,_Kansas "Andover, Kansas"), [Maize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maize,_Kansas "Maize, Kansas"), [Park City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_City,_Kansas "Park City, Kansas"), [Derby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derby,_Kansas "Derby, Kansas"), and [Haysville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haysville,_Kansas "Haysville, Kansas").

Wichita was one of the first cities to add the city commissioner and city manager in their form of government.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-gowichita1-66) Wichita is also home of the nationally recognized [Sedgwick County Zoo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedgwick_County_Zoo "Sedgwick County Zoo").[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-gowichita1-66)

[![Image 25](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/73/Full_Scale_Mercury_Redstone_%282831280402%29.jpg/250px-Full_Scale_Mercury_Redstone_%282831280402%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Full_Scale_Mercury_Redstone_(2831280402).jpg)

The [Cosmosphere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cosmosphere "Cosmosphere"), the world-renowned space museum in Hutchinson

Up river (the [Arkansas River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arkansas_River "Arkansas River")) from Wichita is the city of [Hutchinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hutchinson,_Kansas "Hutchinson, Kansas"). The city was built on one of the world's largest salt deposits (of what would form [Strataca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strataca "Strataca")), and it has the world's largest and longest wheat elevator. It is also the home of [Kansas Cosmosphere and Space Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_Cosmosphere_and_Space_Center "Kansas Cosmosphere and Space Center"), Prairie Dunes Country Club and the [Kansas State Fair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_State_Fair "Kansas State Fair"). North of Wichita along [Interstate 135](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_135_(Kansas) "Interstate 135 (Kansas)") is the city of [Newton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newton,_Kansas "Newton, Kansas"), the former western terminal of the [Santa Fe Railroad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Fe_Railroad "Santa Fe Railroad") and trailhead for the famed [Chisholm Trail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chisholm_Trail "Chisholm Trail"). To the southeast of Wichita are the cities of [Winfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winfield,_Kansas "Winfield, Kansas") and [Arkansas City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arkansas_City,_Kansas "Arkansas City, Kansas") with historic architecture and the [Cherokee Strip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cherokee_Strip_(Kansas) "Cherokee Strip (Kansas)") Museum (in Ark City). The city of [Udall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Udall,_Kansas "Udall, Kansas") was the site of the deadliest [tornado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tornado "Tornado") in Kansas on May 25, 1955; it killed 80 people in and near the city.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-68)

#### Southeast Kansas

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kansas&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Southeast Kansas")]

[![Image 26](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4f/Pittsburg_Kansas_Downtown_Broadway_Fall_2022.jpg/250px-Pittsburg_Kansas_Downtown_Broadway_Fall_2022.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Pittsburg_Kansas_Downtown_Broadway_Fall_2022.jpg)

Pittsburg

[Southeast Kansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southeast_Kansas "Southeast Kansas") has a unique history with a number of nationally registered historic places in this coal-mining region. Located in [Crawford County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crawford_County,_Kansas "Crawford County, Kansas") (dubbed the Fried Chicken Capital of Kansas), [Pittsburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pittsburg,_Kansas "Pittsburg, Kansas") is the largest city in the region and the home of [Pittsburg State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pittsburg_State_University "Pittsburg State University"). The neighboring city of [Frontenac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frontenac,_Kansas "Frontenac, Kansas") in 1888 was the site of the worst mine disaster in the state in which an underground explosion killed 47 miners. "[Big Brutus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Brutus "Big Brutus")" is located 1.5 miles (2.4 km) outside the city of [West Mineral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Mineral,_Kansas "West Mineral, Kansas"). Along with the restored fort, historic [Fort Scott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Scott,_Kansas "Fort Scott, Kansas") has a national cemetery designated by President Lincoln in 1862. The region also shares a Media market with [Joplin, Missouri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joplin,_Missouri "Joplin, Missouri"), a city in Southwest Missouri.

**Kansas** ([/ˈ k æ n z ə s/](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English")[](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/transcoded/e/e9/En-us-Kansas.ogg/En-us-Kansas.ogg.mp3 "Play audio")[ⓘ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:En-us-Kansas.ogg "File:En-us-Kansas.ogg")[_KAN-zəss_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key "Help:Pronunciation respelling key"))[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-11) is a landlocked [state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._state "U.S. state") in the [Midwestern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midwestern_United_States "Midwestern United States") region of the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-12) It borders [Nebraska](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nebraska "Nebraska") to the north, [Colorado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado "Colorado") to the west, [Oklahoma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oklahoma "Oklahoma") to the south, and [Missouri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri "Missouri") to the east. Kansas is named after the [Kansas River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_River "Kansas River"), in turn named after the [Kansa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaw_people "Kaw people") people.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-13)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-14)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-15)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-16) Its [capital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_capitals_in_the_United_States "List of capitals in the United States") is [Topeka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Topeka,_Kansas "Topeka, Kansas"), and its [most populous city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cities_in_Kansas "List of cities in Kansas") is [Wichita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wichita,_Kansas "Wichita, Kansas"); however, the largest urban area is the bi-state [Kansas City metropolitan area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City_metropolitan_area "Kansas City metropolitan area") surrounding [Kansas City, Missouri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City,_Missouri "Kansas City, Missouri"), which straddles the border of Kansas and Missouri.

For thousands of years, what is now known as Kansas was home to numerous and diverse [Indigenous tribes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plains_Indians "Plains Indians"). The first settlement of non-indigenous people in Kansas occurred in 1827 at [Fort Leavenworth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Leavenworth "Fort Leavenworth"). The pace of settlement accelerated in the 1850s, in the midst of political wars over the [slavery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slavery_in_the_United_States "Slavery in the United States") debate. When it was officially opened to settlement by the U.S. government in 1854 with the [Kansas–Nebraska Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas%E2%80%93Nebraska_Act "Kansas–Nebraska Act"), conflict between abolitionist [Free-Staters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free-Stater_(Kansas) "Free-Stater (Kansas)") from [New England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_England "New England") and pro-slavery settlers from neighboring Missouri broke out over the question of whether Kansas would become a [free state or a slave state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slave_states_and_free_states "Slave states and free states"), in a period known as [Bleeding Kansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bleeding_Kansas "Bleeding Kansas"). On January 29, 1861,[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-17)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-18) Kansas entered the [Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Union_(American_Civil_War) "Union (American Civil War)") as a free state, hence the unofficial nickname "The Free State". Passage of the [Homestead Acts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homestead_Acts "Homestead Acts") in 1862 brought a further influx of settlers, and the booming cattle trade of the 1870s attracted some of the Wild West's most iconic figures to western Kansas.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-19)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-20)

As of 2015, Kansas was among the most productive agricultural states, producing high yields of wheat, corn, [sorghum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sorghum "Sorghum"), and [soybeans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soybean "Soybean").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-21) In addition to its traditional strength in agriculture, Kansas possesses an extensive aerospace industry. Kansas, which has an area of 82,278 square miles (213,100 square kilometers) is the [15th-largest state by area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_U.S._states_and_territories_by_area "List of U.S. states and territories by area"), the [36th most-populous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_U.S._states_and_territories_by_population "List of U.S. states and territories by population") of the 50 states, with a population of 2,940,865[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-22) according to the 2020 census, and the [10th least densely populated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_states_and_territories_of_the_United_States_by_population_density "List of states and territories of the United States by population density"). Residents of Kansas are called _Kansans_ or _Jayhawkers_.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-23)[Mount Sunflower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Sunflower "Mount Sunflower") is Kansas's highest point at 4,039 feet (1,231 meters).[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-24)

Kansas is generally considered to be the geographic center of the [contiguous United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contiguous_United_States "Contiguous United States"), with [Lebanon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebanon,_Kansas "Lebanon, Kansas") being [approximately the center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geographic_center_of_the_contiguous_United_States "Geographic center of the contiguous United States").

## Etymology

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kansas&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Etymology")]

![Image 10: Exclamation mark with arrows pointing at each other](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2e/Ambox_contradict.svg/40px-Ambox_contradict.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)This section **appears to contradict itself**. Please see the [talk page](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talk:Kansas# "Talk:Kansas") for more information._(July 2026)_

The name _Kansas_ derives from the [Algonquian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algonquian_languages "Algonquian languages") term _Akansa_, referring to the [Quapaw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quapaw "Quapaw") people. These were a [Dhegiha Siouan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dhegiha_Siouan "Dhegiha Siouan")-speaking people who settled in [Arkansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arkansas "Arkansas") around the 13th century. The stem -_kansa_ is named after the [Kaw people](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaw_people "Kaw people"), also known as the _Kansa_, a federally recognized Native American tribe.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-25) The [tribe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_federally_recognized_tribes "List of federally recognized tribes")'s name (natively _\_kką:ze\__) is often said to mean "people of the (south) wind", although this was probably not the term's original meaning.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-26)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-27)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kansas&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: History")]

Main article: [History of Kansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Kansas "History of Kansas")

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/81/War_dance_in_the_interiour_of_a_Konza_lodge.jpg/250px-War_dance_in_the_interiour_of_a_Konza_lodge.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:War_dance_in_the_interiour_of_a_Konza_lodge.jpg)

Samuel Seymour's 1819 illustration of a [Kansa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaw_people "Kaw people") lodge and dance is the oldest drawing known to have been done in Kansas.

Before [European colonization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_colonization_of_the_Americas "European colonization of the Americas"), Kansas was occupied by the [Caddoan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caddoan "Caddoan")[Wichita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wichita_people "Wichita people") and later the [Siouan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siouan "Siouan")[Kaw people](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaw_people "Kaw people"). The Indigenous people in the eastern part of the state generally lived in villages along the river valleys. Those in the western part of the state were semi-nomadic and hunted large herds of [bison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bison "Bison").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] The first European to set foot in present-day Kansas was the Spanish [conquistador](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conquistador "Conquistador")[Francisco Vázquez de Coronado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francisco_V%C3%A1zquez_de_Coronado "Francisco Vázquez de Coronado"), who explored the area in 1541.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Between 1763 and 1803, the territory of Kansas was integrated into [Spanish Louisiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Louisiana "Spanish Louisiana"). During that period, Governor [Luis de Unzaga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_de_Unzaga "Luis de Unzaga") 'le Conciliateur' promoted expeditions and good relations with the [Amerindians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amerindians "Amerindians"). Explorer Antoine de Marigny and others continued trading across the [Kansas River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_River "Kansas River"), especially at its confluence with the [Missouri River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri_River "Missouri River"), tributaries of the [Mississippi River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mississippi_River "Mississippi River").[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-28)

In 1803, most of modern Kansas was [acquired by the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_territorial_acquisitions "United States territorial acquisitions") as part of the [Louisiana Purchase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisiana_Purchase "Louisiana Purchase"). Southwest Kansas, however, was still a part of Spain, Mexico, and the [Republic of Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_of_Texas "Republic of Texas") until the conclusion of the [Mexican–American War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexican%E2%80%93American_War "Mexican–American War") in 1848, when these lands were [ceded to the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexican_Cession "Mexican Cession"). From 1812 to 1821, Kansas was part of the [Missouri Territory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri_Territory "Missouri Territory"). The [Santa Fe Trail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Fe_Trail "Santa Fe Trail") traversed Kansas from 1821 to 1880, transporting manufactured goods from [Missouri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri "Missouri") and silver and furs from [Santa Fe, New Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Fe,_New_Mexico "Santa Fe, New Mexico"). [Wagon ruts from the trail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Fe_Trail_Remains "Santa Fe Trail Remains") are still visible in the prairie today.

In 1827, [Fort Leavenworth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Leavenworth "Fort Leavenworth") became the first permanent settlement of white Americans in the future state.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-29) The [Kansas–Nebraska Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas%E2%80%93Nebraska_Act "Kansas–Nebraska Act") became law on May 30, 1854, establishing [Nebraska Territory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nebraska_Territory "Nebraska Territory") and [Kansas Territory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_Territory "Kansas Territory"), and opening the area to broader settlement by whites. [Kansas Territory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_Territory "Kansas Territory") stretched all the way to the Continental Divide and included the sites of present-day [Denver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denver "Denver"), [Colorado Springs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs,_Colorado "Colorado Springs, Colorado"), and [Pueblo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pueblo,_Colorado "Pueblo, Colorado").

### Bleeding Kansas and the Civil War

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kansas&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Bleeding Kansas and the Civil War")]

The first non-military settlement of Euro-Americans in Kansas Territory consisted of [abolitionists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abolitionism_in_the_United_States "Abolitionism in the United States") from [Massachusetts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massachusetts "Massachusetts") and other [Free-Staters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free-Stater_(Kansas) "Free-Stater (Kansas)") who founded the town of Lawrence and attempted to stop the spread of slavery from neighboring Missouri.

Missouri and [Arkansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arkansas "Arkansas") continually sent settlers into Kansas Territory along its eastern border to sway votes in favor of slavery prior to Kansas statehood elections. Directly presaging the [American Civil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Civil_War "American Civil War") these forces collided, entering into skirmishes and guerrilla conflicts that earned the territory the nickname [Bleeding Kansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bleeding_Kansas "Bleeding Kansas"). These included [John Brown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Brown_(abolitionist) "John Brown (abolitionist)")'s [Pottawatomie massacre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pottawatomie_massacre "Pottawatomie massacre") of 1856.

Kansas was [admitted to the Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Admission_to_the_Union "Admission to the Union") as a free state on January 29, 1861, making it the 34th state to join the United States. By that time, the violence in Kansas had largely subsided, but during the Civil War, on August 21, 1863, [William Quantrill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Quantrill "William Quantrill") led several hundred of his supporters on a raid into [Lawrence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawrence,_Kansas "Lawrence, Kansas"), destroying much of the city and killing nearly 200 people. He was roundly condemned by both the conventional [Confederate military](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Confederate_States_Army "Confederate States Army") and the partisan rangers commissioned by the [Missouri legislature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri_legislature "Missouri legislature"). His application to that body for a commission was flatly rejected due to his pre-war criminal record.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-30)

### Settlement and the Wild West

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kansas&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Settlement and the Wild West")]

Passage of the [Homestead Acts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homestead_Acts "Homestead Acts") in 1862 accelerated settlement and agricultural development in the state. After the Civil War, many veterans constructed homesteads in Kansas. Many African Americans also looked to Kansas as the land of "[John Brown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Brown_(abolitionist) "John Brown (abolitionist)")" and, led by [freedmen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freedmen "Freedmen") like [Benjamin "Pap" Singleton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benjamin_%22Pap%22_Singleton "Benjamin \"Pap\" Singleton"), began establishing black colonies in the state. Leaving southern states in the late 1870s because of increasing discrimination, they became known as [Exodusters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exodusters "Exodusters").

At the same time, the [Chisholm Trail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chisholm_Trail "Chisholm Trail") was opened and the [Wild West](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Old_West "American Old West") era commenced in Kansas. Storied lawman [Wild Bill Hickok](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wild_Bill_Hickok "Wild Bill Hickok") was a deputy marshal at [Fort Riley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Riley "Fort Riley") and a marshal at [Hays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hays,_Kansas "Hays, Kansas") and [Abilene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abilene,_Kansas "Abilene, Kansas"). [Dodge City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dodge_City,_Kansas "Dodge City, Kansas") was home to both [Bat Masterson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bat_Masterson "Bat Masterson") and [Wyatt Earp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyatt_Earp "Wyatt Earp"), who worked as lawmen in the town. The [Dalton Gang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalton_Gang "Dalton Gang") robbed trains and banks throughout Kansas and the Southwest and maintained a hideout in [Meade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meade,_Kansas "Meade, Kansas"). During its 19th-century peak, Dodge City shipped up to 500,000 Texas cattle annually, cementing its reputation as the "Queen of the Cowtowns".

### 20th century

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kansas&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 20th century")]

In response to demands of [Methodists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Methodists "Methodists") and other [evangelical Protestants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evangelical_Protestants "Evangelical Protestants"), in 1881 Kansas became the first U.S. state to adopt a constitutional amendment [prohibiting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prohibition "Prohibition") all [alcoholic beverages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alcohol_laws_of_Kansas "Alcohol laws of Kansas"), which was repealed in 1948. Anti-saloon activist [Carrie Nation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carrie_Nation "Carrie Nation") vandalized her first saloon in [Kiowa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiowa,_Kansas "Kiowa, Kansas") in 1900. In 1922, suffragist [Ella Uphay Mowry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ella_Uphay_Mowry "Ella Uphay Mowry") became the first female gubernatorial candidate in the state when she ran as "Mrs. W.D. Mowry". She later stated: "Someone had to be the pioneer. I firmly believe that some day a woman will sit in the governor's chair in Kansas."[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-31)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-32)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-33)

Kansas suffered severe environmental damage in the 1930s due to the combined effects of the [Great Depression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Depression "Great Depression") and the [Dust Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dust_Bowl "Dust Bowl"), and large numbers of people left southwestern Kansas in particular for better opportunities elsewhere.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-34) The outbreak of [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II") spurred rapid growth in aircraft manufacturing near Wichita in the so-called [Battle of Kansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Kansas "Battle of Kansas"), and the aerospace sector remains a significant portion of the Kansan economy to this day.

Kansas is bordered by [Nebraska](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nebraska "Nebraska") to the north; [Missouri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri "Missouri") to the east; [Oklahoma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oklahoma "Oklahoma") to the south; and [Colorado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado "Colorado") to the west. The state is divided into [105 counties](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_counties_in_Kansas "List of counties in Kansas") with [628 cities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cities_in_Kansas "List of cities in Kansas"), with its largest county by area being [Butler County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Butler_County,_Kansas "Butler County, Kansas").[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-35) Kansas is located [equidistant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equidistant "Equidistant") from the Pacific and Atlantic oceans. The [geographic center of the 48 contiguous states](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geographic_center_of_the_contiguous_United_States "Geographic center of the contiguous United States") is in [Smith County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smith_County,_Kansas "Smith County, Kansas") near [Lebanon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebanon,_Kansas "Lebanon, Kansas"). Until 1989, the [Meades Ranch Triangulation Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meades_Ranch_Triangulation_Station "Meades Ranch Triangulation Station") in [Osborne County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Osborne_County,_Kansas "Osborne County, Kansas") was the geodetic center of North America: the central reference point for all maps of North America. The geographic center of Kansas is in [Barton County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barton_County,_Kansas "Barton County, Kansas").

### Geology

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kansas&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Geology")]

Main article: [Geology of Kansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geology_of_Kansas "Geology of Kansas")

Kansas is underlain by a sequence of horizontal to gently westward [dipping](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strike_and_dip "Strike and dip")[sedimentary rocks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedimentary_rock "Sedimentary rock"). A sequence of [Mississippian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mississippian_age "Mississippian age"), [Pennsylvanian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pennsylvanian_(geology) "Pennsylvanian (geology)") and [Permian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Permian "Permian") rocks outcrop in the eastern and southern part of the state. The state's western half has exposures of [Cretaceous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cretaceous "Cretaceous") through Tertiary sediments, the latter derived from the [erosion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erosion "Erosion") of the [uplifted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tectonic_uplift "Tectonic uplift")[Rocky Mountains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocky_Mountains "Rocky Mountains") to the west. These are underlain by older Paleozoic and Mesozoic sediments which correlate well with the outcrops to the east. The state's northeastern corner was subjected to [glaciation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glaciation "Glaciation") in the [Pleistocene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pleistocene "Pleistocene") and is covered by [glacial drift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glacial_drift "Glacial drift") and [loess](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loess "Loess").

### Topography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kansas&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Topography")]

The western third of the state, lying in the [great central plain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Plains "Great Plains") of the United States, has a generally flat or undulating surface, while the eastern third has many hills and forests; the middle third is generally hilly, with more sparse vegetation than the eastern third.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-36) The land gradually rises from east to west. Its altitude ranges from 684 ft (208 m) along the [Verdigris River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Verdigris_River "Verdigris River") at [Coffeyville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coffeyville,_Kansas "Coffeyville, Kansas") in [Montgomery County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montgomery_County,_Kansas "Montgomery County, Kansas"), to 4,039 ft (1,231 m) at [Mount Sunflower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Sunflower "Mount Sunflower"), 0.5 miles (0.80 kilometers) from the Colorado border, in [Wallace County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wallace_County,_Kansas "Wallace County, Kansas"). It is a common misconception that Kansas is the flattest state in the nation—in 2003, a tongue-in-cheek study famously declared the state "flatter than a pancake".[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-37) Kansas has a maximum topographic relief of 3,360 ft (1,020 m),[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-38) making it the 23rd flattest U.S. state measured by maximum relief.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-39)
