[Spring River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spring_River_(Missouri) "Spring River (Missouri)"), Kansas

Around 74 mi (119 km) of the state's northeastern boundary is defined by the [Missouri River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri_River "Missouri River"). The [Kansas River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_River "Kansas River") (locally known as the Kaw), formed by the junction of the [Smoky Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smoky_Hill_River "Smoky Hill River") and [Republican](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_River "Republican River") rivers at appropriately named [Junction City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Junction_City,_Kansas "Junction City, Kansas"), joins the Missouri River at [Kansas City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City,_Kansas "Kansas City, Kansas"), after a course of 170 mi (270 km) across the northeastern part of the state.

The [Arkansas River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arkansas_River "Arkansas River") ([pronunciation varies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arkansas_River#Pronunciations "Arkansas River")), rising in [Colorado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado "Colorado"), flows with a bending course for nearly 500 mi (800 km) across the western and southern parts of the state. With its tributaries, (the [Little Arkansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Little_Arkansas_River "Little Arkansas River"), [Ninnescah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ninnescah_River "Ninnescah River"), Walnut, [Cow Creek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cow_Creek_(Kansas) "Cow Creek (Kansas)"), [Cimarron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cimarron_River_(Arkansas_River) "Cimarron River (Arkansas River)"), Verdigris, and the [Neosho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neosho_River "Neosho River")), it forms the southern drainage system of the state.

Kansas's other rivers are the [Saline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saline_River_(Kansas) "Saline River (Kansas)") and Solomon Rivers, tributaries of the Smoky Hill River; the [Big Blue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Blue_River_(Kansas) "Big Blue River (Kansas)"), [Delaware](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delaware_River_(Kansas) "Delaware River (Kansas)"), and [Wakarusa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wakarusa_River "Wakarusa River"), which flow into the Kansas River; and the [Marais des Cygnes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marais_des_Cygnes_River "Marais des Cygnes River"), a tributary of the Missouri River. Spring River is located between [Riverton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverton,_Kansas "Riverton, Kansas") and [Baxter Springs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baxter_Springs,_Kansas "Baxter Springs, Kansas").

In the [Köppen climate classification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K%C3%B6ppen_climate_classification "Köppen climate classification"), Kansas has three climates: humid continental, semi-arid steppe, and humid subtropical. The eastern two-thirds of the state (especially the northeastern portion) has a [humid continental climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humid_continental_climate "Humid continental climate"), with cool to cold winters and hot, often humid summers. Most of the precipitation falls during both the summer and the spring. The [USDA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USDA "USDA")[hardiness zones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hardiness_zone "Hardiness zone") for Kansas range from Zone 5b (−15°F to −10°F) in the North to Zone 7a (0°F to 5°F) in the South.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-46)

The western third of the state—from roughly the [U.S. Route 83](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Route_83 "U.S. Route 83") corridor westward—has a [semi-arid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semi-arid_climate "Semi-arid climate")[steppe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steppe "Steppe") climate. Summers are hot, often very hot, and generally less humid. Winters are highly changeable between warm and very cold. The western region receives an average of about 16 inches (410 millimeters) of precipitation per year. [Chinook winds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinook_wind "Chinook wind") in the winter can warm western Kansas all the way into the 80 degrees Fahrenheit (27 degrees Celsius) range.

The south-central and southeastern portions of the state, including the [Wichita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wichita,_Kansas "Wichita, Kansas") area, have a [humid subtropical climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humid_subtropical_climate "Humid subtropical climate") with hot and humid summers, milder winters, and more precipitation than elsewhere in Kansas. Some features of all three climates can be found in most of the state, with droughts and changeable weather between dry and humid not uncommon, and both warm and cold spells in the winter.

Temperatures in areas between U.S. Routes 83 and [81](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Route_81 "U.S. Route 81"), as well as the southwestern portion of the state along and south of [U.S. 50](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Route_50 "U.S. Route 50"), reach 90°F (32°C) or above on most days of June, July, and August. High humidity added to the high temperatures sends the [heat index](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heat_index "Heat index") into life-threatening territory, especially in Wichita, [Hutchinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hutchinson,_Kansas "Hutchinson, Kansas"), [Salina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salina,_Kansas "Salina, Kansas"), [Russell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russell,_Kansas "Russell, Kansas"), [Hays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hays,_Kansas "Hays, Kansas"), and [Great Bend](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Bend,_Kansas "Great Bend, Kansas"). Temperatures are often higher in [Dodge City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dodge_City,_Kansas "Dodge City, Kansas"), [Garden City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garden_City,_Kansas "Garden City, Kansas"), and [Liberal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberal,_Kansas "Liberal, Kansas"), but the heat index in those three cities is usually lower than the actual air temperature.

Although temperatures of 100°F (38°C) or higher are not as common in areas east of U.S. 81, higher humidity and the [urban heat island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urban_heat_island "Urban heat island") effect lead most summer days to heat indices between 107 and 114°F (42 and 46°C) in [Topeka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Topeka,_Kansas "Topeka, Kansas"), [Lawrence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawrence,_Kansas "Lawrence, Kansas"), and the [Kansas City metropolitan area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City_metropolitan_area "Kansas City metropolitan area"). Also, combined with humidity between 85 and 95 percent, dangerous heat indices can be experienced at every hour of the day.

Precipitation ranges from about 47 inches (1,200 mm) annually in the state's southeast corner to about 16 inches (410 mm) in the southwest. Snowfall ranges from around 5 inches (130 mm) in the fringes of the south, to 35 inches (890 mm) in the far northwest. Frost-free days range from more than 200 days in the south, to 130 days in the northwest. Thus, Kansas is the country's ninth or tenth sunniest state, depending on the source. Western Kansas is as sunny as parts of California and [Arizona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arizona "Arizona").

Kansas is prone to severe weather, especially in the spring and the early-summer. Despite the frequent sunshine throughout much of the state, due to its location at a climatic boundary prone to intrusions of multiple air masses, the state is vulnerable to strong and severe thunderstorms. Some of these storms become [supercell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supercell "Supercell") thunderstorms; these can produce some [tornadoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tornado "Tornado"), occasionally those of [EF3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enhanced_Fujita_scale "Enhanced Fujita scale") strength or higher. Kansas averages more than 50 tornadoes annually.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-Annual_Average_Number_of_Tornadoes-47) Severe thunderstorms sometimes drop some very large [hail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hail "Hail") over Kansas as well. Furthermore, these storms can even bring in flash flooding and damaging straight line winds.

According to NOAA, the all-time highest temperature recorded in Kansas is (121°F or 49.4°C) on July 24, 1936, near [Alton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alton,_Kansas "Alton, Kansas") in [Osborne County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Osborne_County,_Kansas "Osborne County, Kansas"), and the all-time low is −40°F (−40°C) on February 13, 1905, near [Lebanon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebanon,_Kansas "Lebanon, Kansas") in [Smith County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smith_County,_Kansas "Smith County, Kansas"). Alton and Lebanon are approximately 50 miles (80 km) apart.

Kansas's record high of 121°F (49.4°C) ties with [North Dakota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Dakota "North Dakota") for the fifth-highest record high in an American state, behind California (134°F or 56.7°C), [Arizona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arizona "Arizona") (128°F or 53.3°C), [Nevada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nevada "Nevada") (125°F or 51.7°C), and [New Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico "New Mexico") (122°F or 50°C).

Known as [rural flight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rural_flight "Rural flight"), the last few decades have been marked by a migratory pattern out of the countryside into cities. Out of all the cities in these Midwestern states, 89% have fewer than 3,000 people, and hundreds of those have fewer than 1,000. In Kansas alone, there are more than 6,000 [ghost towns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ghost_towns_in_Kansas "List of ghost towns in Kansas") and dwindling communities,[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-49) according to one Kansas historian, Daniel C. Fitzgerald. At the same time, some of the communities in Johnson County (metropolitan Kansas City) are among the fastest-growing in the country.

Kansas has 627 [incorporated cities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Municipal_corporation "Municipal corporation"). By state statute, cities are divided into three classes as determined by the population obtained "by any census of enumeration". A city of the third class has a population of less than 5,000, but cities reaching a population of more than 2,000 may be certified as a city of the second class. The second class is limited to cities with a population of less than 25,000, and upon reaching a population of more than 15,000, they may be certified as a city of the first class. First and second class cities are independent of any [township](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_township "Civil township") and are not included within the township's territory.

### Life expectancy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kansas&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Life expectancy")]

The residents of Kansas have a life expectancy near the U.S. national average. In 2013, males in Kansas lived an average of 76.6 years compared to a male national average of 76.7 years and females lived an average of 81.0 years compared to a female national average of 81.5 years. Increases in life expectancy between 1980 and 2013 were below the national average for males and near the national average for females. Male life expectancy in Kansas between 1980 and 2014 increased by an average of 5.2 years, compared to a male national average of a 6.7-year increase. Life expectancy for females in Kansas between 1980 and 2014 increased by 4.3 years, compared to a female national average of a 4.0 year increase.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-61)

Using 2017–2019 data, the [Robert Wood Johnson Foundation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Wood_Johnson_Foundation "Robert Wood Johnson Foundation") calculated that life expectancy for Kansas counties ranged from 75.8 years for [Wyandotte County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyandotte_County,_Kansas "Wyandotte County, Kansas") to 81.7 years for [Johnson County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnson_County,_Kansas "Johnson County, Kansas"). Life expectancy for the state as a whole was 78.5 years.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-Robert_Wood_Johnson-62) Life expectancy for the United States as a whole in 2019 was 78.8 years.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-Mortality-63)

#### Northeast Kansas

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kansas&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Northeast Kansas")]

[![Image 22](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/69/UK_Strong_Hall_Lawrence_Nima_02.jpg/250px-UK_Strong_Hall_Lawrence_Nima_02.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:UK_Strong_Hall_Lawrence_Nima_02.jpg)

[University of Kansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Kansas "University of Kansas") Strong Hall in Lawrence

The northeastern portion of the state, extending from the eastern border to [Junction City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Junction_City,_Kansas "Junction City, Kansas") and from the Nebraska border to south of Johnson County is home to more than 1.5 million people in the Kansas City (Kansas portion), Manhattan, Lawrence, and Topeka [metropolitan areas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_area "Metropolitan area"). [Overland Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overland_Park,_Kansas "Overland Park, Kansas"), a young city incorporated in 1960, has the largest population and the largest land area in the county. It is home to [Johnson County Community College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnson_County_Community_College "Johnson County Community College").

Olathe is the [county seat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_seat "County seat") and home to [Johnson County Executive Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnson_County_Executive_Airport "Johnson County Executive Airport"). The cities of Olathe, [Shawnee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawnee,_Kansas "Shawnee, Kansas"), [De Soto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/De_Soto,_Kansas "De Soto, Kansas") and [Gardner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gardner,_Kansas "Gardner, Kansas") have some of the state's fastest growing populations. The cities of Overland Park, [Lenexa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lenexa,_Kansas "Lenexa, Kansas"), Olathe, De Soto, and Gardner are also notable because they lie along the former route of the [Santa Fe Trail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Fe_Trail "Santa Fe Trail"). Among cities with at least one thousand residents, [Mission Hills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mission_Hills,_Kansas "Mission Hills, Kansas") has the highest median income in the state.

Several institutions of higher education are located in Northeast Kansas including [Baker University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baker_University "Baker University") (the oldest university in the state, founded in 1858 and affiliated with the [United Methodist Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Methodist_Church "United Methodist Church")) in Baldwin City, [Benedictine College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benedictine_College "Benedictine College") (sponsored by [St. Benedict's Abbey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Benedict's_Abbey "St. Benedict's Abbey") and [Mount St. Scholastica Monastery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benedictine_Sisters_of_Mount_St._Scholastica "Benedictine Sisters of Mount St. Scholastica") and formed from the merger of St. Benedict's College (1858) and Mount St. Scholastica College (1923)) in Atchison, [MidAmerica Nazarene University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MidAmerica_Nazarene_University "MidAmerica Nazarene University") in Olathe, [Ottawa University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ottawa_University "Ottawa University") in Ottawa and Overland Park, Kansas City Kansas Community College and KU Medical Center in Kansas City, and KU Edwards Campus in Overland Park. Less than an hour's drive to the west, [Lawrence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawrence,_Kansas "Lawrence, Kansas") is home to the [University of Kansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Kansas "University of Kansas"), the largest public university in the state, and [Haskell Indian Nations University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haskell_Indian_Nations_University "Haskell Indian Nations University").

To the north, [Kansas City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City,_Kansas "Kansas City, Kansas"), with the second-largest land area in the state, contains a number of diverse ethnic neighborhoods. Its attractions include the [Kansas Speedway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_Speedway "Kansas Speedway"), [Sporting Kansas City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sporting_Kansas_City "Sporting Kansas City"), [Kansas City Monarchs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City_Monarchs_(American_Association) "Kansas City Monarchs (American Association)"), and [The Legends at Village West](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legends_at_Village_West "The Legends at Village West") retail and entertainment center. Nearby, Kansas's first settlement [Bonner Springs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bonner_Springs,_Kansas "Bonner Springs, Kansas")[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-autogenerated1-64) is home to several national and regional attractions including the [Providence Medical Center Amphitheater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cricket_Wireless_Amphitheater_(Bonner_Springs,_Kansas) "Cricket Wireless Amphitheater (Bonner Springs, Kansas)"), the [National Agricultural Center and Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Agricultural_Center_and_Hall_of_Fame "National Agricultural Center and Hall of Fame"), and the annual [Kansas City Renaissance Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City_Renaissance_Festival "Kansas City Renaissance Festival"). Further up the [Missouri River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri_River "Missouri River"), the city of [Lansing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lansing,_Kansas "Lansing, Kansas") is the home of the state's first maximum-security prison. Historic [Leavenworth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leavenworth,_Kansas "Leavenworth, Kansas"), founded in 1854, was the first incorporated city in Kansas. North of the city, [Fort Leavenworth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Leavenworth "Fort Leavenworth") is the oldest active Army post west of the [Mississippi River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mississippi_River "Mississippi River"). The city of [Atchison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atchison,_Kansas "Atchison, Kansas") was an early commercial center in the state and is well known as the birthplace of [Amelia Earhart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amelia_Earhart "Amelia Earhart").

[![Image 23](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/08/Kansas_State_Capitol_in_summer_2024.jpg/250px-Kansas_State_Capitol_in_summer_2024.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kansas_State_Capitol_in_summer_2024.jpg)

The [Kansas Statehouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_Statehouse "Kansas Statehouse")

To the west, nearly a quarter million people reside in the Topeka metropolitan area. [Topeka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Topeka,_Kansas "Topeka, Kansas") is the state capital and home to [Washburn University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washburn_University "Washburn University") and [Washburn Institute of Technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washburn_Institute_of_Technology "Washburn Institute of Technology"). Built at a [Kansas River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_River "Kansas River") crossing along the old [Oregon Trail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oregon_Trail "Oregon Trail"), this historic city has several nationally registered historic places. Further westward along [Interstate 70](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_70_(Kansas) "Interstate 70 (Kansas)") and the Kansas River is [Junction City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Junction_City,_Kansas "Junction City, Kansas") with its historic limestone and brick buildings and nearby [Fort Riley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Riley "Fort Riley"), well known as the home to the [U.S. Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Army "United States Army")'s [1st Infantry Division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1st_Infantry_Division_(United_States) "1st Infantry Division (United States)") (nicknamed "the Big Red One"). A short distance away, the city of [Manhattan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manhattan,_Kansas "Manhattan, Kansas") is home to [Kansas State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_State_University "Kansas State University"), the second-largest public university in the state and the nation's oldest land-grant university, dating back to 1863. South of the campus, [Aggieville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aggieville "Aggieville") dates back to 1889 and is the state's oldest shopping district of its kind.

Downtown Wichita in the winter

In south-central Kansas, the [Wichita metropolitan area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wichita_metropolitan_area,_Kansas "Wichita metropolitan area, Kansas") is home to more than 600,000 people.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-65)[Wichita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wichita,_Kansas "Wichita, Kansas") is the largest city in the state in terms of both land area and population. 'The Air Capital' is a major manufacturing center for the aircraft industry and the home of [Wichita State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wichita_State_University "Wichita State University"). Before Wichita was 'The Air Capital' it was a Cowtown.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-gowichita1-66) With a number of nationally registered historic places, museums, and other entertainment destinations, it has a desire to become a cultural mecca in the Midwest. Wichita's population growth has grown by double digits and the surrounding suburbs are among the fastest growing cities in the state. The population of [Goddard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goddard,_Kansas "Goddard, Kansas") has grown by more than 11% per year since 2000.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-2006SubEst-67) Other fast-growing cities include [Andover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andover,_Kansas "Andover, Kansas"), [Maize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maize,_Kansas "Maize, Kansas"), [Park City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_City,_Kansas "Park City, Kansas"), [Derby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derby,_Kansas "Derby, Kansas"), and [Haysville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haysville,_Kansas "Haysville, Kansas").

Wichita was one of the first cities to add the city commissioner and city manager in their form of government.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-gowichita1-66) Wichita is also home of the nationally recognized [Sedgwick County Zoo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedgwick_County_Zoo "Sedgwick County Zoo").[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-gowichita1-66)

Up river (the [Arkansas River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arkansas_River "Arkansas River")) from Wichita is the city of [Hutchinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hutchinson,_Kansas "Hutchinson, Kansas"). The city was built on one of the world's largest salt deposits (of what would form [Strataca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strataca "Strataca")), and it has the world's largest and longest wheat elevator. It is also the home of [Kansas Cosmosphere and Space Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_Cosmosphere_and_Space_Center "Kansas Cosmosphere and Space Center"), Prairie Dunes Country Club and the [Kansas State Fair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_State_Fair "Kansas State Fair"). North of Wichita along [Interstate 135](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_135_(Kansas) "Interstate 135 (Kansas)") is the city of [Newton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newton,_Kansas "Newton, Kansas"), the former western terminal of the [Santa Fe Railroad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Fe_Railroad "Santa Fe Railroad") and trailhead for the famed [Chisholm Trail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chisholm_Trail "Chisholm Trail"). To the southeast of Wichita are the cities of [Winfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winfield,_Kansas "Winfield, Kansas") and [Arkansas City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arkansas_City,_Kansas "Arkansas City, Kansas") with historic architecture and the [Cherokee Strip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cherokee_Strip_(Kansas) "Cherokee Strip (Kansas)") Museum (in Ark City). The city of [Udall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Udall,_Kansas "Udall, Kansas") was the site of the deadliest [tornado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tornado "Tornado") in Kansas on May 25, 1955; it killed 80 people in and near the city.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas#cite_note-68)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

(Redirected from [Dinosaur tracks](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dinosaur_tracks&redirect=no "Dinosaur tracks"))

Fossilized footprint (ichnite)

[![Image 4](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/42/JialingpusYuechiensis%28Ichnite%29-PaleozoologicalMuseumOfChina-May23-08.jpg/250px-JialingpusYuechiensis%28Ichnite%29-PaleozoologicalMuseumOfChina-May23-08.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:JialingpusYuechiensis(Ichnite)-PaleozoologicalMuseumOfChina-May23-08.jpg)

A reverse ichnite of the impression of _Jialingpus yuechiensis_, on display at the [Paleozoological Museum of China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paleozoological_Museum_of_China "Paleozoological Museum of China")

A **fossil [track](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal_track "Animal track")** or **ichnite** ([Greek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancient_Greek "Ancient Greek") "_ἴχνιον_" (_ichnion_) – a track, trace or footstep) is a fossilized [footprint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Footprint "Footprint"). This is a type of [trace fossil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trace_fossil "Trace fossil"). A **fossil trackway** is a sequence of fossil tracks left by a single organism. Over the years, many ichnites have been found, around the world, giving important clues about the behaviour (and foot structure and stride) of the animals that made them. For instance, multiple ichnites of a single species, close together, suggest 'herd' or 'pack' behaviour of that species.

Combinations of footprints of different species provide clues about the interactions of those species. Even a set of footprints of a single animal gives important clues, as to whether it was [bipedal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biped "Biped") or [quadrupedal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quadruped "Quadruped"). In this way, it has been suggested that some [pterosaurs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pterosaur "Pterosaur"), when on the ground, used their forelimbs in an unexpected quadrupedal action.

Special conditions are required, in order to preserve a footprint made in soft ground (such as an [alluvial plain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alluvial_plain "Alluvial plain") or a formative [sedimentary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedimentary_rock "Sedimentary rock") deposit). A possible scenario is a sea or lake shore that became dried out to a firm mud in hot, dry conditions, received the footprints (because it would only have been partially hardened and the animal would have been heavy) and then became silted over in a flash storm.

The first ichnite found was in 1800 in Massachusetts, US, by a farmer named Pliny Moody, who found 1-foot (31 cm) long fossilized footprints. They were thought by Harvard and Yale scholars to be from "Noah's Raven".[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-1)

A famous group of ichnites was found in a limestone quarry at [Ardley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ardley,_Oxfordshire "Ardley, Oxfordshire"), 20 km Northeast of [Oxford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxford "Oxford"), [England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/England "England"), in 1997. They were thought to have been made by _[Megalosaurus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Megalosaurus "Megalosaurus")_ and possibly _[Cetiosaurus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cetiosaurus "Cetiosaurus")_. There are replicas of some of these footprints, set across the lawn of [Oxford University Museum of Natural History](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxford_University_Museum_of_Natural_History "Oxford University Museum of Natural History") (OUMNH).

A creature named _[Cheirotherium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chirotherium "Chirotherium")_ was, for a long time and still may be, only known from its fossilized trail. Its footprints were first found in 1834, in [Thuringia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thuringia "Thuringia"), [Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany "Germany"), dating from the Late [Triassic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Triassic "Triassic")[Period](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Period_(geology) "Period (geology)").

The largest known dinosaur footprints, belonging to [sauropods](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sauropoda "Sauropoda") and dating from the early [Cretaceous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cretaceous "Cretaceous") were found to the north of [Broome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broome,_Western_Australia "Broome, Western Australia") on the [Dampier Peninsula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dampier_Peninsula "Dampier Peninsula"), [Western Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Australia "Western Australia"), with some footprints measuring 1.7 m.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-3) The 3D digital documentation of tracks has the benefit of being able to examine ichnite in detail remotely and distribute the data to colleagues and other interested personnel.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-4)

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/82/Protichnites.jpg/250px-Protichnites.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Protichnites.jpg)

Fossil trackway _[Protichnites](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protichnites "Protichnites")_ in sedimentary stone

## Fossil trackways

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fossil_track&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Fossil trackways")]

Many fossil trackways were made by [dinosaurs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosauria "Dinosauria"), early [tetrapods](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tetrapod "Tetrapod"), and other [quadrupeds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quadruped "Quadruped") and [bipeds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biped "Biped") on land. Marine organisms also made many ancient trackways (such as the trails of [trilobites](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trilobite "Trilobite") and [eurypterids](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eurypterid "Eurypterid") like _[Hibbertopterus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hibbertopterus "Hibbertopterus")_).

Some basic fossil trackway types:

1.   footprints
2.   tail drags
3.   belly drag marks – (e.g., tetrapods)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-5)
4.   chain of trace platforms – (example: _[Yorgia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yorgia "Yorgia")_)
5.   body imprint – ([Monuron trackway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monuron_trackway?action=edit&redlink=1 "Monuron trackway (page does not exist)"), insect)

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/24/Yorgia_trace.jpg/250px-Yorgia_trace.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Yorgia_trace.jpg)

Specialized marine trace trackway, [Yorgia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yorgia "Yorgia"), from the [Ediacaran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ediacaran "Ediacaran") of northern Russia

The majority of fossil trackways are [foot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foot "Foot") impressions on land, or subsurface water, but other types of creatures will leave distinctive impressions. Examples of creatures supported, or partially supported, in a [water](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Water "Water") environment are known. The fossil "[millipede](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Millipede "Millipede")-type" genus _[Arthropleura](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthropleura "Arthropleura")_ left its multi-legged/feet trackways on land.

### Hominid trackways

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fossil_track&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Hominid trackways")]

#### Africa

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fossil_track&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Africa")]

##### Tanzania

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fossil_track&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Tanzania")]

See also: [Laetoli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laetoli "Laetoli")

[![Image 7](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/5/5f/Laetoli.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail_unscaled)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Laetoli.jpg)

Laetoli Site, February 2006

Some of the earliest trackways for human ancestors have been discovered in [Tanzania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanzania "Tanzania").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-:1-6) The [Laetoli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laetoli "Laetoli") trackway is famous for the [hominin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hominin "Hominin") footprints preserved in [volcanic ash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volcanic_ash "Volcanic ash"). After the footprints were made in powdery ash, soft rain cemented the ash layer into [tuff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tuff "Tuff"), preserving the prints.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-:1-6) The hominid prints were produced by three individuals, one walking in the footprints of the other, making the original tracks difficult to discover. As the tracks lead in the same direction, they might have been produced by a group – but there is nothing else to support the common reconstruction of a nuclear family visiting the waterhole together.

##### South Africa

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fossil_track&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: South Africa")]

In [South Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Africa "South Africa"), two ancient trackways have been found containing footprints, one at Langebaan and one at Nahoon. Both trackways occur in calcareous eolianites or hardened sand dunes. At Nahoon, trackways of at least five species of vertebrates, including three hominid footprints, are preserved as casts.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-7) The prints at [Langebaan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Langebaan "Langebaan") are the oldest human footprints, dated to approximately 117,000 years old.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-8)

Twenty six human fossil trackways have been found in the Willandra Lakes area adjacent to Lake Garnpung, consisting of 563 human footprints from 19,000 to 20,000 years ago.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-Willandra-9)

### Early Tetrapod

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fossil_track&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Early Tetrapod")]

The earliest land creatures (actually land-marine coastal-riverine-marshland) left some of the first terrestrial trackways. They range from tetrapods to proto-reptilians and others.

A possible first connection of a trackway with the vertebrate that left it was published by Drs. Sebastian Voigt and David Berman and Amy Henrici in the 12 September 2007 issue of _[Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Journal\_of\_Vertebrate\_Paleontology "Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology")_. The paleontologists who made the connection were aided by unusually detailed trackways left in fine-grained [Lower Permian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Permian "Permian") mud of the Tambach Formation in central Germany, together with exceptionally complete fossilised skeletons in the same 290-million-year-old strata. They matched the two most common trackways with the two most common fossils, two reptile-like herbivores known as _[Diadectes absitus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diadectes "Diadectes")_ (with the trackway pseudonym _Ichniotherium cottae_) and _[Orobates pabsti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orobates "Orobates")_ (with the trackway pseudonym of _Orobates pabsti_).[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-10)

The Permo-[Carboniferous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carboniferous "Carboniferous") of [Prince Edward Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prince_Edward_Island "Prince Edward Island"), Canada contains trackways of tetrapods and stem-reptiles.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-11) Macrofloral and [palynological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palynology "Palynology") information help date them.

Ireland hosts late Middle [Devonian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devonian "Devonian") tetrapod trackways at three sites on [Valentia Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valentia_Island "Valentia Island") within the Valentia Slate Formation.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-13)

The earliest fossil trackway of primitive tetrapods in Australia occurs in the [Genoa River Gorge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genoa,_Victoria "Genoa, Victoria"), Victoria, dating from the [Devonian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devonian "Devonian") 350 million years ago.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-14)

### Dinosaur trackways

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fossil_track&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Dinosaur trackways")]

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a8/First_Dinosaur_Tracks_from_the_Arabian_Peninsula.jpg/250px-First_Dinosaur_Tracks_from_the_Arabian_Peninsula.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:First_Dinosaur_Tracks_from_the_Arabian_Peninsula.jpg)

[Arabian Peninsula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arabian_Peninsula "Arabian Peninsula") dinosaur trackway 

Dinosaurs lived on the continents before [grasses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grass "Grass") evolved (the "Age of the Grasses" evolved with the "Age of the Mammals"); the dinosaurs lived in the [Triassic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Triassic "Triassic"), [Jurassic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jurassic "Jurassic"), and [Cretaceous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cretaceous "Cretaceous") and left many trackways, both from plant-eaters and the meat-eaters, in various layers of mud and sand.

With scientific analysis, dinosaur specialists are now analyzing tracks for the _**walking-speeds**_, or _sprint_-_**running speeds**_ for all categories of dinosaurs, even to the large plant eaters, but especially the faster 3-toed meat hunters. _Evidence of_ _**herding**_, as well as _**pack hunting**_ are also being investigated.

#### Bolivia

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fossil_track&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Bolivia")]

*   [Cal Orck'o](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cal_Orck'o "Cal Orck'o"), Cretaceous park, [Sucre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sucre "Sucre"), Bolivia
*   From an investigation that began in the 1960s, it wasn't until December 2025 that paleontologists from Loma Linda University in California discovered 16,600 footprints left by theropods, the dinosaur group that includes the [Tyrannosaurus rex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tyrannosaurus_rex "Tyrannosaurus rex"). After six years of regular field visits, this finding sets the highest number of theropod footprints ever discovered in the world. The footprint sizes indicated that giant creatures roughly 10 meters (33 feet) tall, while also finding tiny theropod footprints the size of a chicken, 32 centimeters (1 foot) tall at the hip. Interestingly enough, the scientist who found it in 1960 wanted to prove to kids that those prints weren't made by a monster, but by a dinosaur.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-15)

#### Brazil

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fossil_track&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Brazil")]

##### Namibia

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fossil_track&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Namibia")]

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/50/Dinosaurstracks_Otjihaenamaparero_Namibia.JPG/250px-Dinosaurstracks_Otjihaenamaparero_Namibia.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Dinosaurstracks_Otjihaenamaparero_Namibia.JPG)

Dinosaur trace fossil of Otjihaenamparero

In north-central Namibia there is a dinosaur trackway in sandstone on what is now the private farm [Otjihaenamparero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Otjihaenamparero "Otjihaenamparero"). Larger footprints are of a [ceratosauria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ceratosauria "Ceratosauria") and smaller ones of [syntarsus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coelophysis "Coelophysis"). The prints are believed to be around 190 million years old.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-17)

##### Zimbabwe

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fossil_track&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Zimbabwe")]

In the Lower Zimbabwe Rift Valley there is a trackway in 140 Ma rose-coloured [sandstone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandstone "Sandstone") of Chewore Area. The small footprint size, with both [manus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manus_(zoology) "Manus (zoology)") and [pes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pes_(zoology) "Pes (zoology)"), implies that it is a trackway of a juvenile, a probable [carnosaur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carnosaur "Carnosaur").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-18)

#### North America

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fossil_track&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: North America")]

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bd/DilophosaurusByPhilKonstantin.jpg/250px-DilophosaurusByPhilKonstantin.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:DilophosaurusByPhilKonstantin.jpg)

Probable _Dilophosaurus_ footprint from Red Fleet State Park, northeastern Utah

The western regions of North America, especially the western border of the [Western Interior Seaway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Interior_Seaway "Western Interior Seaway"), are common for dinosaur trackways. [Wyoming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming "Wyoming") has dinosaur trackways from the Late Cretaceous, 65 ma.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-19) (A model example of this 3-toed Wyoming trackway was made for presentation.)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-20)

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a8/Paluxy_River.jpg/250px-Paluxy_River.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Paluxy_River.jpg)

Theropod and sauropod tracks under water in the Paluxy River

In the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States"), [dinosaur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur "Dinosaur") footprints and trackways are found in the [Glen Rose Formation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glen_Rose_Formation "Glen Rose Formation"), the most famous of these being the [Paluxy River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paluxy_River "Paluxy River") site in [Dinosaur Valley State Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_Valley_State_Park "Dinosaur Valley State Park"). These were the first [sauropoda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sauropoda "Sauropoda") footprints scientifically documented, and were designated a US [National Natural Landmark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Natural_Landmark "National Natural Landmark") in 1969. Some are as large as about 3 feet across. The prints are thought to have been preserved originally in a [tidal flat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tidal_flat "Tidal flat") or a [lagoon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagoon "Lagoon").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-Lockley-21) There are tracks from two types of dinosaur. The first type of tracks are from a [sauropod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sauropoda "Sauropoda") and were made by an animal of 30 to 50 feet in length, perhaps a [brachiosaurid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brachiosaurid "Brachiosaurid") such as _[Pleurocoelus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pleurocoelus "Pleurocoelus")_,[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-Lockley-21) and the second tracks by a [theropoda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theropoda "Theropoda"), an animal of 20 to 30 feet in length, perhaps an _[Acrocanthosaurus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acrocanthosaurus "Acrocanthosaurus")_. A variety of scenarios was proposed to explain the tracks, but most likely represent twelve sauropods "probably as a herd, followed somewhat later by three theropods that may or may not have been stalking – but that certainly were not attacking."[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-Lockley-21)

Other examples include:

*   Dinosaur tracks, near [Moab, Utah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moab,_Utah "Moab, Utah")[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-22)
*   [Dinosaur Footprints Reservation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_Footprints_Reservation "Dinosaur Footprints Reservation") in [Holyoke, Massachusetts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holyoke,_Massachusetts "Holyoke, Massachusetts"), US
*   [Red Gulch Dinosaur Tracksite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Gulch_Dinosaur_Tracksite "Red Gulch Dinosaur Tracksite"), Wyoming
*   [Prehistoric Trackways National Monument](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prehistoric_Trackways_National_Monument "Prehistoric Trackways National Monument") near [Las Cruces, New Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Cruces,_New_Mexico "Las Cruces, New Mexico")
*   [Connecticut River Valley trackways](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Connecticut_River_Valley_trackways "Connecticut River Valley trackways"), in New England
*   [Clayton Lake State Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clayton_Lake_State_Park "Clayton Lake State Park") dinosaur trackway near [Clayton, New Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clayton,_New_Mexico "Clayton, New Mexico")
*   West Gold Hill Dinosaur Track in [Uncompahgre National Forest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uncompahgre_National_Forest "Uncompahgre National Forest") near [Ouray, Colorado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ouray,_Colorado "Ouray, Colorado")

#### Asia

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fossil_track&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Asia")]

##### China

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fossil_track&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: China")]

The Gansu dinosaur trackway located in the Liujiazia National Dinosaur Geopark in Yanguoxia, China contains hundreds of tracks including 245 dinosaur, 350 theropod, 364 sauropod and 628 ornithopod tracks among others.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-Gansu-23)

##### Thailand

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fossil_track&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Thailand")]

The [Phu Pha Man National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phu_Pha_Man_National_Park "Phu Pha Man National Park") in [Thailand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thailand "Thailand") contains one of the oldest dinosaur tracks to have been discovered in [Asia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asia "Asia").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-24) Discovered in January 2024, paleontologists from the [Department of Mineral Resources](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Department_of_Mineral_Resources_(Thailand) "Department of Mineral Resources (Thailand)") have dated the tracks to around 225–220 million years old (the late Triassic period).[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-25) The track contains traces of a variety of dinosaurs including theropods, sauropods, and archosaurs.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-26)

#### Australia

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fossil_track&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: Australia")]

The [Lark Quarry Trackway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lark_Quarry_Dinosaur_Trackways "Lark Quarry Dinosaur Trackways") in [Queensland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queensland "Queensland") contains three-toed tracks made by a herd of [ornithopod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ornithopoda "Ornithopoda") dinosaurs crossing a river. It was once believed they respresented a large predator chasing a mixed flock of small ornithopods and theropods, but this was contested in 2011.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-:0-27)

##### Portugal

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fossil_track&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Portugal")]

*   [Lagosteiros Natural Monument](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagosteiros_Natural_Monument "Lagosteiros Natural Monument"), in [Sesimbra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sesimbra "Sesimbra"), with [theropod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theropod "Theropod") and [ornithopod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ornithopod "Ornithopod") tracks from the [Early Cretaceous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_Cretaceous "Early Cretaceous").
*   [Aire Range Dinosaur Tracks Natural Monument](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aire_Range_Dinosaur_Tracks_Natural_Monument "Aire Range Dinosaur Tracks Natural Monument") near [Torres Novas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Torres_Novas "Torres Novas"). In 1994 about 20 [sauropod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sauropod "Sauropod") trackways from the [Middle Jurassic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle_Jurassic "Middle Jurassic") were discovered in the _Pedreira do Galinha_ quarry.

##### England

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fossil_track&action=edit&section=22 "Edit section: England")]

In a [Bathonian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bathonian "Bathonian")[limestone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limestone "Limestone") quarry site at [Ardley, Oxfordshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ardley,_Oxfordshire "Ardley, Oxfordshire") more than 40 sets of footprints, with some trackways reaching up to 180 metres in length, were discovered in 1997. These prints are largely only preserved in replicas and photographic records due to quarrying and subsequent restoration. Theropod tracks have been tentatively assigned to the [ichnogenus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ichnogenus "Ichnogenus")[Megalosauripus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Megalosauripus "Megalosauripus"), possibly from [Megalosaurus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Megalosaurus#Later_finds_of_Megalosaurus_bucklandii "Megalosaurus"). The sauropod tracks could be grouped into _wide-gauge_ trackways, associated with early [titanosauria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titanosauria "Titanosauria") or [brachiosauridae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brachiosauridae "Brachiosauridae"), and _narrow-gauge_ ones, possibly from [Cetiosaurus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cetiosaurus#Later_species "Cetiosaurus") or a basal [diplodocoid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diplodocoid "Diplodocoid").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-28) In 2024 at nearby [Dewars Farm Quarry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dewars_Farm_Quarry "Dewars Farm Quarry"),[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-29) five new extensive [Middle Jurassic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle_Jurassic "Middle Jurassic") trackways dating back about 166 Ma were discovered, with evidence of more in the neighbourhood. The longest continuous trackway measured more than 150 metres. Four of the trackways were made by large [sauropods](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sauropods "Sauropods"), most likely again _Cetiosaurus_. The fifth one was identified as made by the carnivorous [theropod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theropod "Theropod")_Megalosaurus_, based on its distinctive three-toed feet with claws. One area of the site shows the carnivore and herbivore tracks crossing over, suggesting the predator followed up on the steps of the sauropod.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-30)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-31)

### Mammal trackways

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fossil_track&action=edit&section=23 "Edit section: Mammal trackways")]

Mammal trackways are among the least common trackways. Mammals were not often in mud, or riverine environments; they were more often in forestlands or grasslands. Thus the earlier tetrapods or proto-tetrapods would yield the most fossil trackways. The [Walchia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walchia "Walchia") forest of [Brule, Nova Scotia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brule,_Nova_Scotia "Brule, Nova Scotia") has an example of an [in situ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_situ "In situ") Walchia forest, and tetrapod trackways that extended over some period of time through the forest area.

#### United States

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fossil_track&action=edit&section=24 "Edit section: United States")]

A 1.5km-long Late Pleistocene Age trackway of human (child and adult) fossilized footprints, as well as [mammoth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mammoth "Mammoth") and [giant ground sloth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giant_ground_sloth "Giant ground sloth") tracks have been found at [White Sands National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Sands_footprints "White Sands footprints") near [Alamogordo, New Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alamogordo,_New_Mexico "Alamogordo, New Mexico").[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-Las_Cruces_Sun_News-32)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-QSR-33)

#### Australia

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fossil_track&action=edit&section=25 "Edit section: Australia")]

A recent [marsupial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marsupial "Marsupial") trackway site at [Colac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colac,_Victoria "Colac, Victoria") in the [Australian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australia "Australia") state of [Victoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victoria_(state) "Victoria (state)") contains marsupial trackways as well as kangaroo and wallaby tracks.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-34)

### Pterosaur trackways

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fossil_track&action=edit&section=26 "Edit section: Pterosaur trackways")]

#### France

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fossil_track&action=edit&section=27 "Edit section: France")]

[Pterosaur Beach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pterosaur_Beach "Pterosaur Beach") was, at the end of the [Jurassic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jurassic "Jurassic") era, a [mudflat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mudflat "Mudflat"), flooded at high tide, on a marine lagoon in a [gulf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf "Gulf") that opened on the [Atlantic Ocean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_Ocean "Atlantic Ocean") between [Bordeaux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bordeaux "Bordeaux") and the island of [Oléron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ol%C3%A9ron "Oléron"). On it, animals foraged for food.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-35) The site has hundreds of fossilized trackways.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-36)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

(Redirected from [Dinosaur tracks](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dinosaur_tracks&redirect=no "Dinosaur tracks"))

Fossilized footprint (ichnite)

[![Image 4](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/42/JialingpusYuechiensis%28Ichnite%29-PaleozoologicalMuseumOfChina-May23-08.jpg/250px-JialingpusYuechiensis%28Ichnite%29-PaleozoologicalMuseumOfChina-May23-08.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:JialingpusYuechiensis(Ichnite)-PaleozoologicalMuseumOfChina-May23-08.jpg)

A reverse ichnite of the impression of _Jialingpus yuechiensis_, on display at the [Paleozoological Museum of China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paleozoological_Museum_of_China "Paleozoological Museum of China")

A **fossil [track](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal_track "Animal track")** or **ichnite** ([Greek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancient_Greek "Ancient Greek") "_ἴχνιον_" (_ichnion_) – a track, trace or footstep) is a fossilized [footprint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Footprint "Footprint"). This is a type of [trace fossil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trace_fossil "Trace fossil"). A **fossil trackway** is a sequence of fossil tracks left by a single organism. Over the years, many ichnites have been found, around the world, giving important clues about the behaviour (and foot structure and stride) of the animals that made them. For instance, multiple ichnites of a single species, close together, suggest 'herd' or 'pack' behaviour of that species.

Combinations of footprints of different species provide clues about the interactions of those species. Even a set of footprints of a single animal gives important clues, as to whether it was [bipedal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biped "Biped") or [quadrupedal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quadruped "Quadruped"). In this way, it has been suggested that some [pterosaurs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pterosaur "Pterosaur"), when on the ground, used their forelimbs in an unexpected quadrupedal action.

Special conditions are required, in order to preserve a footprint made in soft ground (such as an [alluvial plain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alluvial_plain "Alluvial plain") or a formative [sedimentary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedimentary_rock "Sedimentary rock") deposit). A possible scenario is a sea or lake shore that became dried out to a firm mud in hot, dry conditions, received the footprints (because it would only have been partially hardened and the animal would have been heavy) and then became silted over in a flash storm.

The first ichnite found was in 1800 in Massachusetts, US, by a farmer named Pliny Moody, who found 1-foot (31 cm) long fossilized footprints. They were thought by Harvard and Yale scholars to be from "Noah's Raven".[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-1)

A famous group of ichnites was found in a limestone quarry at [Ardley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ardley,_Oxfordshire "Ardley, Oxfordshire"), 20 km Northeast of [Oxford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxford "Oxford"), [England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/England "England"), in 1997. They were thought to have been made by _[Megalosaurus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Megalosaurus "Megalosaurus")_ and possibly _[Cetiosaurus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cetiosaurus "Cetiosaurus")_. There are replicas of some of these footprints, set across the lawn of [Oxford University Museum of Natural History](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxford_University_Museum_of_Natural_History "Oxford University Museum of Natural History") (OUMNH).

A creature named _[Cheirotherium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chirotherium "Chirotherium")_ was, for a long time and still may be, only known from its fossilized trail. Its footprints were first found in 1834, in [Thuringia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thuringia "Thuringia"), [Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany "Germany"), dating from the Late [Triassic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Triassic "Triassic")[Period](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Period_(geology) "Period (geology)").

The largest known dinosaur footprints, belonging to [sauropods](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sauropoda "Sauropoda") and dating from the early [Cretaceous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cretaceous "Cretaceous") were found to the north of [Broome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broome,_Western_Australia "Broome, Western Australia") on the [Dampier Peninsula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dampier_Peninsula "Dampier Peninsula"), [Western Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Australia "Western Australia"), with some footprints measuring 1.7 m.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-3) The 3D digital documentation of tracks has the benefit of being able to examine ichnite in detail remotely and distribute the data to colleagues and other interested personnel.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-4)

## Fossil trackways

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fossil_track&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Fossil trackways")]

Many fossil trackways were made by [dinosaurs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosauria "Dinosauria"), early [tetrapods](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tetrapod "Tetrapod"), and other [quadrupeds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quadruped "Quadruped") and [bipeds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biped "Biped") on land. Marine organisms also made many ancient trackways (such as the trails of [trilobites](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trilobite "Trilobite") and [eurypterids](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eurypterid "Eurypterid") like _[Hibbertopterus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hibbertopterus "Hibbertopterus")_).

Some basic fossil trackway types:

1.   footprints
2.   tail drags
3.   belly drag marks – (e.g., tetrapods)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-5)
4.   chain of trace platforms – (example: _[Yorgia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yorgia "Yorgia")_)
5.   body imprint – ([Monuron trackway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monuron_trackway?action=edit&redlink=1 "Monuron trackway (page does not exist)"), insect)

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/24/Yorgia_trace.jpg/250px-Yorgia_trace.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Yorgia_trace.jpg)

Specialized marine trace trackway, [Yorgia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yorgia "Yorgia"), from the [Ediacaran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ediacaran "Ediacaran") of northern Russia

The majority of fossil trackways are [foot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foot "Foot") impressions on land, or subsurface water, but other types of creatures will leave distinctive impressions. Examples of creatures supported, or partially supported, in a [water](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Water "Water") environment are known. The fossil "[millipede](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Millipede "Millipede")-type" genus _[Arthropleura](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthropleura "Arthropleura")_ left its multi-legged/feet trackways on land.

#### Africa

##### Tanzania

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fossil_track&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Tanzania")]

See also: [Laetoli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laetoli "Laetoli")

[![Image 7](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/5/5f/Laetoli.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail_unscaled)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Laetoli.jpg)

Laetoli Site, February 2006

Some of the earliest trackways for human ancestors have been discovered in [Tanzania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanzania "Tanzania").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-:1-6) The [Laetoli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laetoli "Laetoli") trackway is famous for the [hominin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hominin "Hominin") footprints preserved in [volcanic ash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volcanic_ash "Volcanic ash"). After the footprints were made in powdery ash, soft rain cemented the ash layer into [tuff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tuff "Tuff"), preserving the prints.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-:1-6) The hominid prints were produced by three individuals, one walking in the footprints of the other, making the original tracks difficult to discover. As the tracks lead in the same direction, they might have been produced by a group – but there is nothing else to support the common reconstruction of a nuclear family visiting the waterhole together.

##### South Africa

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fossil_track&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: South Africa")]

In [South Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Africa "South Africa"), two ancient trackways have been found containing footprints, one at Langebaan and one at Nahoon. Both trackways occur in calcareous eolianites or hardened sand dunes. At Nahoon, trackways of at least five species of vertebrates, including three hominid footprints, are preserved as casts.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-7) The prints at [Langebaan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Langebaan "Langebaan") are the oldest human footprints, dated to approximately 117,000 years old.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-8)

### Early Tetrapod

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fossil_track&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Early Tetrapod")]

The earliest land creatures (actually land-marine coastal-riverine-marshland) left some of the first terrestrial trackways. They range from tetrapods to proto-reptilians and others.

A possible first connection of a trackway with the vertebrate that left it was published by Drs. Sebastian Voigt and David Berman and Amy Henrici in the 12 September 2007 issue of _[Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Journal\_of\_Vertebrate\_Paleontology "Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology")_. The paleontologists who made the connection were aided by unusually detailed trackways left in fine-grained [Lower Permian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Permian "Permian") mud of the Tambach Formation in central Germany, together with exceptionally complete fossilised skeletons in the same 290-million-year-old strata. They matched the two most common trackways with the two most common fossils, two reptile-like herbivores known as _[Diadectes absitus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diadectes "Diadectes")_ (with the trackway pseudonym _Ichniotherium cottae_) and _[Orobates pabsti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orobates "Orobates")_ (with the trackway pseudonym of _Orobates pabsti_).[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-10)

The Permo-[Carboniferous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carboniferous "Carboniferous") of [Prince Edward Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prince_Edward_Island "Prince Edward Island"), Canada contains trackways of tetrapods and stem-reptiles.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-11) Macrofloral and [palynological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palynology "Palynology") information help date them.

Ireland hosts late Middle [Devonian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devonian "Devonian") tetrapod trackways at three sites on [Valentia Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valentia_Island "Valentia Island") within the Valentia Slate Formation.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-13)

The earliest fossil trackway of primitive tetrapods in Australia occurs in the [Genoa River Gorge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genoa,_Victoria "Genoa, Victoria"), Victoria, dating from the [Devonian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devonian "Devonian") 350 million years ago.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-14)

### Dinosaur trackways

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fossil_track&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Dinosaur trackways")]

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a8/First_Dinosaur_Tracks_from_the_Arabian_Peninsula.jpg/250px-First_Dinosaur_Tracks_from_the_Arabian_Peninsula.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:First_Dinosaur_Tracks_from_the_Arabian_Peninsula.jpg)

[Arabian Peninsula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arabian_Peninsula "Arabian Peninsula") dinosaur trackway 

Dinosaurs lived on the continents before [grasses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grass "Grass") evolved (the "Age of the Grasses" evolved with the "Age of the Mammals"); the dinosaurs lived in the [Triassic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Triassic "Triassic"), [Jurassic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jurassic "Jurassic"), and [Cretaceous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cretaceous "Cretaceous") and left many trackways, both from plant-eaters and the meat-eaters, in various layers of mud and sand.

With scientific analysis, dinosaur specialists are now analyzing tracks for the _**walking-speeds**_, or _sprint_-_**running speeds**_ for all categories of dinosaurs, even to the large plant eaters, but especially the faster 3-toed meat hunters. _Evidence of_ _**herding**_, as well as _**pack hunting**_ are also being investigated.

#### Bolivia

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fossil_track&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Bolivia")]

*   [Cal Orck'o](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cal_Orck'o "Cal Orck'o"), Cretaceous park, [Sucre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sucre "Sucre"), Bolivia
*   From an investigation that began in the 1960s, it wasn't until December 2025 that paleontologists from Loma Linda University in California discovered 16,600 footprints left by theropods, the dinosaur group that includes the [Tyrannosaurus rex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tyrannosaurus_rex "Tyrannosaurus rex"). After six years of regular field visits, this finding sets the highest number of theropod footprints ever discovered in the world. The footprint sizes indicated that giant creatures roughly 10 meters (33 feet) tall, while also finding tiny theropod footprints the size of a chicken, 32 centimeters (1 foot) tall at the hip. Interestingly enough, the scientist who found it in 1960 wanted to prove to kids that those prints weren't made by a monster, but by a dinosaur.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-15)
