##### Namibia

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fossil_track&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Namibia")]

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/50/Dinosaurstracks_Otjihaenamaparero_Namibia.JPG/250px-Dinosaurstracks_Otjihaenamaparero_Namibia.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Dinosaurstracks_Otjihaenamaparero_Namibia.JPG)

Dinosaur trace fossil of Otjihaenamparero

In north-central Namibia there is a dinosaur trackway in sandstone on what is now the private farm [Otjihaenamparero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Otjihaenamparero "Otjihaenamparero"). Larger footprints are of a [ceratosauria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ceratosauria "Ceratosauria") and smaller ones of [syntarsus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coelophysis "Coelophysis"). The prints are believed to be around 190 million years old.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-17)

##### Zimbabwe

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fossil_track&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Zimbabwe")]

In the Lower Zimbabwe Rift Valley there is a trackway in 140 Ma rose-coloured [sandstone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandstone "Sandstone") of Chewore Area. The small footprint size, with both [manus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manus_(zoology) "Manus (zoology)") and [pes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pes_(zoology) "Pes (zoology)"), implies that it is a trackway of a juvenile, a probable [carnosaur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carnosaur "Carnosaur").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-18)

#### North America

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fossil_track&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: North America")]

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bd/DilophosaurusByPhilKonstantin.jpg/250px-DilophosaurusByPhilKonstantin.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:DilophosaurusByPhilKonstantin.jpg)

Probable _Dilophosaurus_ footprint from Red Fleet State Park, northeastern Utah

The western regions of North America, especially the western border of the [Western Interior Seaway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Interior_Seaway "Western Interior Seaway"), are common for dinosaur trackways. [Wyoming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming "Wyoming") has dinosaur trackways from the Late Cretaceous, 65 ma.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-19) (A model example of this 3-toed Wyoming trackway was made for presentation.)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-20)

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a8/Paluxy_River.jpg/250px-Paluxy_River.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Paluxy_River.jpg)

Theropod and sauropod tracks under water in the Paluxy River

In the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States"), [dinosaur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur "Dinosaur") footprints and trackways are found in the [Glen Rose Formation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glen_Rose_Formation "Glen Rose Formation"), the most famous of these being the [Paluxy River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paluxy_River "Paluxy River") site in [Dinosaur Valley State Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_Valley_State_Park "Dinosaur Valley State Park"). These were the first [sauropoda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sauropoda "Sauropoda") footprints scientifically documented, and were designated a US [National Natural Landmark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Natural_Landmark "National Natural Landmark") in 1969. Some are as large as about 3 feet across. The prints are thought to have been preserved originally in a [tidal flat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tidal_flat "Tidal flat") or a [lagoon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagoon "Lagoon").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-Lockley-21) There are tracks from two types of dinosaur. The first type of tracks are from a [sauropod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sauropoda "Sauropoda") and were made by an animal of 30 to 50 feet in length, perhaps a [brachiosaurid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brachiosaurid "Brachiosaurid") such as _[Pleurocoelus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pleurocoelus "Pleurocoelus")_,[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-Lockley-21) and the second tracks by a [theropoda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theropoda "Theropoda"), an animal of 20 to 30 feet in length, perhaps an _[Acrocanthosaurus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acrocanthosaurus "Acrocanthosaurus")_. A variety of scenarios was proposed to explain the tracks, but most likely represent twelve sauropods "probably as a herd, followed somewhat later by three theropods that may or may not have been stalking – but that certainly were not attacking."[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-Lockley-21)

Other examples include:

*   Dinosaur tracks, near [Moab, Utah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moab,_Utah "Moab, Utah")[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-22)
*   [Dinosaur Footprints Reservation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_Footprints_Reservation "Dinosaur Footprints Reservation") in [Holyoke, Massachusetts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holyoke,_Massachusetts "Holyoke, Massachusetts"), US
*   [Red Gulch Dinosaur Tracksite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Gulch_Dinosaur_Tracksite "Red Gulch Dinosaur Tracksite"), Wyoming
*   [Prehistoric Trackways National Monument](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prehistoric_Trackways_National_Monument "Prehistoric Trackways National Monument") near [Las Cruces, New Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Cruces,_New_Mexico "Las Cruces, New Mexico")
*   [Connecticut River Valley trackways](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Connecticut_River_Valley_trackways "Connecticut River Valley trackways"), in New England
*   [Clayton Lake State Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clayton_Lake_State_Park "Clayton Lake State Park") dinosaur trackway near [Clayton, New Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clayton,_New_Mexico "Clayton, New Mexico")
*   West Gold Hill Dinosaur Track in [Uncompahgre National Forest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uncompahgre_National_Forest "Uncompahgre National Forest") near [Ouray, Colorado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ouray,_Colorado "Ouray, Colorado")

#### Asia

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fossil_track&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Asia")]

##### China

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fossil_track&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: China")]

The Gansu dinosaur trackway located in the Liujiazia National Dinosaur Geopark in Yanguoxia, China contains hundreds of tracks including 245 dinosaur, 350 theropod, 364 sauropod and 628 ornithopod tracks among others.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-Gansu-23)

##### Thailand

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fossil_track&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Thailand")]

The [Phu Pha Man National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phu_Pha_Man_National_Park "Phu Pha Man National Park") in [Thailand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thailand "Thailand") contains one of the oldest dinosaur tracks to have been discovered in [Asia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asia "Asia").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-24) Discovered in January 2024, paleontologists from the [Department of Mineral Resources](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Department_of_Mineral_Resources_(Thailand) "Department of Mineral Resources (Thailand)") have dated the tracks to around 225–220 million years old (the late Triassic period).[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-25) The track contains traces of a variety of dinosaurs including theropods, sauropods, and archosaurs.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-26)

#### Australia

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fossil_track&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: Australia")]

The [Lark Quarry Trackway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lark_Quarry_Dinosaur_Trackways "Lark Quarry Dinosaur Trackways") in [Queensland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queensland "Queensland") contains three-toed tracks made by a herd of [ornithopod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ornithopoda "Ornithopoda") dinosaurs crossing a river. It was once believed they respresented a large predator chasing a mixed flock of small ornithopods and theropods, but this was contested in 2011.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-:0-27)

#### Europe

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fossil_track&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Europe")]

##### Portugal

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fossil_track&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Portugal")]

*   [Lagosteiros Natural Monument](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagosteiros_Natural_Monument "Lagosteiros Natural Monument"), in [Sesimbra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sesimbra "Sesimbra"), with [theropod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theropod "Theropod") and [ornithopod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ornithopod "Ornithopod") tracks from the [Early Cretaceous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_Cretaceous "Early Cretaceous").
*   [Aire Range Dinosaur Tracks Natural Monument](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aire_Range_Dinosaur_Tracks_Natural_Monument "Aire Range Dinosaur Tracks Natural Monument") near [Torres Novas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Torres_Novas "Torres Novas"). In 1994 about 20 [sauropod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sauropod "Sauropod") trackways from the [Middle Jurassic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle_Jurassic "Middle Jurassic") were discovered in the _Pedreira do Galinha_ quarry.

##### England

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fossil_track&action=edit&section=22 "Edit section: England")]

In a [Bathonian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bathonian "Bathonian")[limestone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limestone "Limestone") quarry site at [Ardley, Oxfordshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ardley,_Oxfordshire "Ardley, Oxfordshire") more than 40 sets of footprints, with some trackways reaching up to 180 metres in length, were discovered in 1997. These prints are largely only preserved in replicas and photographic records due to quarrying and subsequent restoration. Theropod tracks have been tentatively assigned to the [ichnogenus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ichnogenus "Ichnogenus")[Megalosauripus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Megalosauripus "Megalosauripus"), possibly from [Megalosaurus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Megalosaurus#Later_finds_of_Megalosaurus_bucklandii "Megalosaurus"). The sauropod tracks could be grouped into _wide-gauge_ trackways, associated with early [titanosauria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titanosauria "Titanosauria") or [brachiosauridae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brachiosauridae "Brachiosauridae"), and _narrow-gauge_ ones, possibly from [Cetiosaurus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cetiosaurus#Later_species "Cetiosaurus") or a basal [diplodocoid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diplodocoid "Diplodocoid").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-28) In 2024 at nearby [Dewars Farm Quarry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dewars_Farm_Quarry "Dewars Farm Quarry"),[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-29) five new extensive [Middle Jurassic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle_Jurassic "Middle Jurassic") trackways dating back about 166 Ma were discovered, with evidence of more in the neighbourhood. The longest continuous trackway measured more than 150 metres. Four of the trackways were made by large [sauropods](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sauropods "Sauropods"), most likely again _Cetiosaurus_. The fifth one was identified as made by the carnivorous [theropod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theropod "Theropod")_Megalosaurus_, based on its distinctive three-toed feet with claws. One area of the site shows the carnivore and herbivore tracks crossing over, suggesting the predator followed up on the steps of the sauropod.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-30)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-31)

### Mammal trackways

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fossil_track&action=edit&section=23 "Edit section: Mammal trackways")]

Mammal trackways are among the least common trackways. Mammals were not often in mud, or riverine environments; they were more often in forestlands or grasslands. Thus the earlier tetrapods or proto-tetrapods would yield the most fossil trackways. The [Walchia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walchia "Walchia") forest of [Brule, Nova Scotia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brule,_Nova_Scotia "Brule, Nova Scotia") has an example of an [in situ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_situ "In situ") Walchia forest, and tetrapod trackways that extended over some period of time through the forest area.

#### United States

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fossil_track&action=edit&section=24 "Edit section: United States")]

A 1.5km-long Late Pleistocene Age trackway of human (child and adult) fossilized footprints, as well as [mammoth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mammoth "Mammoth") and [giant ground sloth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giant_ground_sloth "Giant ground sloth") tracks have been found at [White Sands National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Sands_footprints "White Sands footprints") near [Alamogordo, New Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alamogordo,_New_Mexico "Alamogordo, New Mexico").[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-Las_Cruces_Sun_News-32)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-QSR-33)

#### Australia

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fossil_track&action=edit&section=25 "Edit section: Australia")]

A recent [marsupial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marsupial "Marsupial") trackway site at [Colac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colac,_Victoria "Colac, Victoria") in the [Australian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australia "Australia") state of [Victoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victoria_(state) "Victoria (state)") contains marsupial trackways as well as kangaroo and wallaby tracks.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-34)

### Pterosaur trackways

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fossil_track&action=edit&section=26 "Edit section: Pterosaur trackways")]

#### France

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fossil_track&action=edit&section=27 "Edit section: France")]

[Pterosaur Beach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pterosaur_Beach "Pterosaur Beach") was, at the end of the [Jurassic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jurassic "Jurassic") era, a [mudflat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mudflat "Mudflat"), flooded at high tide, on a marine lagoon in a [gulf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf "Gulf") that opened on the [Atlantic Ocean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_Ocean "Atlantic Ocean") between [Bordeaux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bordeaux "Bordeaux") and the island of [Oléron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ol%C3%A9ron "Oléron"). On it, animals foraged for food.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-35) The site has hundreds of fossilized trackways.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_tracks#cite_note-36)

**Ardley** is a village and [civil parish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_parishes_in_England "Civil parishes in England") in [Oxfordshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxfordshire "Oxfordshire"), England, about 4 miles (6.4 km) northwest of [Bicester](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bicester "Bicester"). The parish includes the village of **Fewcott**, which is now contiguous with Ardley.

The [2021 Census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom_Census_2021 "United Kingdom Census 2021") recorded the population of Ardley parish as 740.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ardley,_Oxfordshire#cite_note-1)

## Geography and natural history

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ardley,_Oxfordshire&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Geography and natural history")]

The two villages of Ardley and Fewcott are on either side of a stream that rises at [Fritwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fritwell "Fritwell"), flows south to Ardley, then turns east through [Stoke Lyne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stoke_Lyne "Stoke Lyne") to [Fringford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fringford "Fringford"). There it joins Crowell Brook, which continues east into [Buckinghamshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buckinghamshire "Buckinghamshire") and ultimately becomes part of the [Great Ouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/River_Great_Ouse "River Great Ouse").

The [limestone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cotswold_stone "Cotswold stone")[quarry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quarry "Quarry") at Ardley has yielded a significant find of [dinosaur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur "Dinosaur") tracks ([ichnites](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ichnite "Ichnite")), discovered in 1997 and thought to have been left by [Megalosaurus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Megalosaurus "Megalosaurus") and possibly [Cetiosaurus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cetiosaurus "Cetiosaurus"). Some of these are on display in the dinosaur garden at the [Oxfordshire Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Oxfordshire_Museum "The Oxfordshire Museum") in [Woodstock, Oxfordshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woodstock,_Oxfordshire "Woodstock, Oxfordshire").

There is a [site of special scientific interest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Site_of_special_scientific_interest "Site of special scientific interest") in the village with a colony of the [great crested newts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_crested_newt "Great crested newt") and an outcrop of [Jurassic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jurassic "Jurassic") limestone.

## Castle

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ardley,_Oxfordshire&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Castle")]

[Ardley Castle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ardley_Castle "Ardley Castle") is a [motte-and-bailey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motte-and-bailey "Motte-and-bailey") which is believed to have been built early in the 12th century during the [civil war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Anarchy#Conflict_between_Stephen_and_Matilda "The Anarchy") between [Empress Matilda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Empress_Matilda "Empress Matilda") and [King Stephen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_of_England "Stephen of England").

## Parish church

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ardley,_Oxfordshire&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Parish church")]

The [Church of England parish church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Church_of_England_parish_church "Church of England parish church") of [Saint Mary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary_(mother_of_Jesus) "Mary (mother of Jesus)") dates from at least 1074.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ardley,_Oxfordshire#cite_note-2) The original church was demolished and completely rebuilt, but both the [chancel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chancel "Chancel") and the [bell tower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bell_tower "Bell tower") of the present building contain small amounts of re-used [Norman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norman_architecture "Norman architecture") stonework. The present [Early English Gothic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_Gothic_architecture#Early_English_Gothic "English Gothic architecture") chancel was built late in the 12th or early in the 13th century. The tower has a [saddleback roof](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saddleback_roof "Saddleback roof") and may have been built in the 13th or 14th century. The present [nave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nave "Nave") was built in 1793 and has a [west gallery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_gallery_music "West gallery music") that was added in 1834.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ardley,_Oxfordshire#cite_note-3)

St Mary's is now part of the [Benefice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benefice#Church_of_England "Benefice") of Cherwell Valley, along with the parishes of Fritwell, [Lower Heyford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lower_Heyford "Lower Heyford"), [Somerton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Somerton,_Oxfordshire "Somerton, Oxfordshire"), [Souldern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Church_of_the_Annunciation_to_the_Blessed_Virgin_Mary,_Souldern "Church of the Annunciation to the Blessed Virgin Mary, Souldern") and [Upper Heyford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upper_Heyford,_Oxfordshire "Upper Heyford, Oxfordshire").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ardley,_Oxfordshire#cite_note-4)

The [canal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canals_of_the_United_Kingdom "Canals of the United Kingdom") engineer [Samuel Simcock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samuel_Simcock?action=edit&redlink=1 "Samuel Simcock (page does not exist)") (1727–1804) and his wife Esther (1720–1808), a sister of [James Brindley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Brindley "James Brindley"), are buried at St Mary's.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ardley,_Oxfordshire#cite_note-5)

## Economic history

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ardley,_Oxfordshire&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Economic history")]

In 1910 the [Great Western Railway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Western_Railway "Great Western Railway") completed a [new main line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chiltern_Main_Line#The_Bicester_cut-off "Chiltern Main Line") linking [Ashendon Junction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashendon_Junction "Ashendon Junction") and [Aynho Junction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aynho_Junction "Aynho Junction") to shorten the high-speed route between its termini at [London Paddington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_Paddington_railway_station "London Paddington railway station") and [Birmingham Snow Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birmingham_Snow_Hill_railway_station "Birmingham Snow Hill railway station"). The line passes within a few hundred yards of Ardley and the GWR opened a railway station on the main road just south of the village. [British Railways](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Rail "British Rail") closed [Ardley railway station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ardley_railway_station "Ardley railway station") in 1963. The railway remains open and is now part of the [Chiltern Main Line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chiltern_Main_Line "Chiltern Main Line").

In 1990 the section of the [M40 motorway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M40_motorway "M40 motorway") between [Wheatley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wheatley,_Oxfordshire "Wheatley, Oxfordshire") and [Hockley Heath](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hockley_Heath "Hockley Heath") was built. M40 Junction 10 with the [A43 road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A43_road "A43 road") is about 550 yards (500 m) northeast of Ardley and its [Cherwell Valley services](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cherwell_Valley_services "Cherwell Valley services") are about 1,100 yards (1 km) from the village.

## Amenities

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ardley,_Oxfordshire&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Amenities")]

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4e/Ardley_Fox%26Hounds_%26_barn.JPG/250px-Ardley_Fox%26Hounds_%26_barn.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ardley_Fox&Hounds_&_barn.JPG)

The Fox and Hounds

Ardley formerly had a [public house](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_house "Public house"), the Fox and Hounds, which closed its doors in January 2020.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ardley,_Oxfordshire#cite_note-6) Fewcott does have a pub, the White Lion Inn, located on Fritwell Road.

The village has no shops. Those at Cherwell Valley services (Junction 10 of the M40) are the nearest to the village.

[Ardley United Football Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ardley_United_F.C. "Ardley United F.C.")[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ardley,_Oxfordshire#cite_note-7) is a [Non-League football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-League_football "Non-League football") club whose first team plays its home games at The Playing Fields. Its first team is in the [FTL Futbol Hellenic League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hellenic_Football_League "Hellenic Football League") Premier Division.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ardley,_Oxfordshire#cite_note-8)

**Ardley** is a village and [civil parish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_parishes_in_England "Civil parishes in England") in [Oxfordshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxfordshire "Oxfordshire"), England, about 4 miles (6.4 km) northwest of [Bicester](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bicester "Bicester"). The parish includes the village of **Fewcott**, which is now contiguous with Ardley.

The [2021 Census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom_Census_2021 "United Kingdom Census 2021") recorded the population of Ardley parish as 740.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ardley,_Oxfordshire#cite_note-1)

## Geography and natural history

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ardley,_Oxfordshire&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Geography and natural history")]

The two villages of Ardley and Fewcott are on either side of a stream that rises at [Fritwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fritwell "Fritwell"), flows south to Ardley, then turns east through [Stoke Lyne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stoke_Lyne "Stoke Lyne") to [Fringford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fringford "Fringford"). There it joins Crowell Brook, which continues east into [Buckinghamshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buckinghamshire "Buckinghamshire") and ultimately becomes part of the [Great Ouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/River_Great_Ouse "River Great Ouse").

The [limestone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cotswold_stone "Cotswold stone")[quarry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quarry "Quarry") at Ardley has yielded a significant find of [dinosaur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur "Dinosaur") tracks ([ichnites](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ichnite "Ichnite")), discovered in 1997 and thought to have been left by [Megalosaurus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Megalosaurus "Megalosaurus") and possibly [Cetiosaurus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cetiosaurus "Cetiosaurus"). Some of these are on display in the dinosaur garden at the [Oxfordshire Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Oxfordshire_Museum "The Oxfordshire Museum") in [Woodstock, Oxfordshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woodstock,_Oxfordshire "Woodstock, Oxfordshire").

There is a [site of special scientific interest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Site_of_special_scientific_interest "Site of special scientific interest") in the village with a colony of the [great crested newts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_crested_newt "Great crested newt") and an outcrop of [Jurassic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jurassic "Jurassic") limestone.

## Castle

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ardley,_Oxfordshire&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Castle")]

[Ardley Castle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ardley_Castle "Ardley Castle") is a [motte-and-bailey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motte-and-bailey "Motte-and-bailey") which is believed to have been built early in the 12th century during the [civil war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Anarchy#Conflict_between_Stephen_and_Matilda "The Anarchy") between [Empress Matilda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Empress_Matilda "Empress Matilda") and [King Stephen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_of_England "Stephen of England").

## Parish church

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ardley,_Oxfordshire&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Parish church")]

The [Church of England parish church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Church_of_England_parish_church "Church of England parish church") of [Saint Mary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary_(mother_of_Jesus) "Mary (mother of Jesus)") dates from at least 1074.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ardley,_Oxfordshire#cite_note-2) The original church was demolished and completely rebuilt, but both the [chancel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chancel "Chancel") and the [bell tower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bell_tower "Bell tower") of the present building contain small amounts of re-used [Norman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norman_architecture "Norman architecture") stonework. The present [Early English Gothic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_Gothic_architecture#Early_English_Gothic "English Gothic architecture") chancel was built late in the 12th or early in the 13th century. The tower has a [saddleback roof](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saddleback_roof "Saddleback roof") and may have been built in the 13th or 14th century. The present [nave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nave "Nave") was built in 1793 and has a [west gallery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_gallery_music "West gallery music") that was added in 1834.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ardley,_Oxfordshire#cite_note-3)

St Mary's is now part of the [Benefice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benefice#Church_of_England "Benefice") of Cherwell Valley, along with the parishes of Fritwell, [Lower Heyford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lower_Heyford "Lower Heyford"), [Somerton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Somerton,_Oxfordshire "Somerton, Oxfordshire"), [Souldern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Church_of_the_Annunciation_to_the_Blessed_Virgin_Mary,_Souldern "Church of the Annunciation to the Blessed Virgin Mary, Souldern") and [Upper Heyford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upper_Heyford,_Oxfordshire "Upper Heyford, Oxfordshire").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ardley,_Oxfordshire#cite_note-4)

The [canal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canals_of_the_United_Kingdom "Canals of the United Kingdom") engineer [Samuel Simcock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samuel_Simcock?action=edit&redlink=1 "Samuel Simcock (page does not exist)") (1727–1804) and his wife Esther (1720–1808), a sister of [James Brindley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Brindley "James Brindley"), are buried at St Mary's.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ardley,_Oxfordshire#cite_note-5)

## Economic history

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ardley,_Oxfordshire&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Economic history")]

In 1910 the [Great Western Railway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Western_Railway "Great Western Railway") completed a [new main line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chiltern_Main_Line#The_Bicester_cut-off "Chiltern Main Line") linking [Ashendon Junction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashendon_Junction "Ashendon Junction") and [Aynho Junction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aynho_Junction "Aynho Junction") to shorten the high-speed route between its termini at [London Paddington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_Paddington_railway_station "London Paddington railway station") and [Birmingham Snow Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birmingham_Snow_Hill_railway_station "Birmingham Snow Hill railway station"). The line passes within a few hundred yards of Ardley and the GWR opened a railway station on the main road just south of the village. [British Railways](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Rail "British Rail") closed [Ardley railway station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ardley_railway_station "Ardley railway station") in 1963. The railway remains open and is now part of the [Chiltern Main Line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chiltern_Main_Line "Chiltern Main Line").

In 1990 the section of the [M40 motorway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M40_motorway "M40 motorway") between [Wheatley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wheatley,_Oxfordshire "Wheatley, Oxfordshire") and [Hockley Heath](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hockley_Heath "Hockley Heath") was built. M40 Junction 10 with the [A43 road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A43_road "A43 road") is about 550 yards (500 m) northeast of Ardley and its [Cherwell Valley services](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cherwell_Valley_services "Cherwell Valley services") are about 1,100 yards (1 km) from the village.

## Amenities

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ardley,_Oxfordshire&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Amenities")]

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4e/Ardley_Fox%26Hounds_%26_barn.JPG/250px-Ardley_Fox%26Hounds_%26_barn.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ardley_Fox&Hounds_&_barn.JPG)

The Fox and Hounds

Ardley formerly had a [public house](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_house "Public house"), the Fox and Hounds, which closed its doors in January 2020.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ardley,_Oxfordshire#cite_note-6) Fewcott does have a pub, the White Lion Inn, located on Fritwell Road.

The village has no shops. Those at Cherwell Valley services (Junction 10 of the M40) are the nearest to the village.

[Ardley United Football Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ardley_United_F.C. "Ardley United F.C.")[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ardley,_Oxfordshire#cite_note-7) is a [Non-League football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-League_football "Non-League football") club whose first team plays its home games at The Playing Fields. Its first team is in the [FTL Futbol Hellenic League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hellenic_Football_League "Hellenic Football League") Premier Division.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ardley,_Oxfordshire#cite_note-8)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

Dinosaur fossil trackway

[![Image 5](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/74/Megapnosaurus_.tif/lossy-page1-250px-Megapnosaurus_.tif.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Megapnosaurus_.tif)

_[Grallator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grallator "Grallator")_ footprints made by a trackmaker similar to _[Coelophysis rhodesiensis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coelophysis\_rhodesiensis "Coelophysis rhodesiensis")_, found at the St. George Dinosaur Discovery Site. 

[![Image 6](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4e/Gigandipus.JPG/330px-Gigandipus.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Gigandipus.JPG)

[Gigandipus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gigandipus "Gigandipus") footprint at the site

The **St. George Dinosaur Discovery Site** is a fossil site and museum at Johnson Farm in [Saint George](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_George,_Utah "Saint George, Utah"), [Utah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Utah "Utah").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._George_Dinosaur_Discovery_Site#cite_note-History-1) The museum preserves thousands of dinosaur footprints right at the original site of discovery.

The site was discovered by accident on February 26, 2000 by Dr. Sheldon Johnson, a retired optometrist and resident of St. George. He was in the process of excavating his property when he stumbled upon a large, naturally cut rock. The rock exposed a natural [dinosaur footprint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_footprint "Dinosaur footprint"), which Johnson originally thought to be a complete dinosaur fossil due to the quality of the preservation.

Realizing that these dinosaur tracks would be best served if they were maintained for scientific and educational purposes, Dr. Johnson and his wife, LaVerna, worked to set aside the land and its fossils. Eventually the Johnsons donated the tracks that had been found and arranged for the land to be cared for by the City of St. George. They worked with scientists, local businesses, and government officials on the local, state, and national levels to create the museum which opened in 2005 and is here today. They set up the foundation that continues to preserve the site as a creative learning environment.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._George_Dinosaur_Discovery_Site#cite_note-History-1)

The best preserved and most numerous tracks today form the in-place trackway and exhibits of the St. George Dinosaur Discovery Site. Many other fossils including bones of dinosaurs and fish, shells of small aquatic animals, and leaves and seeds of plants, have joined the footprints, enabling palaeontologists to reconstruct the nearly 200 million-year-old ecosystem preserved here with unprecedented clarity, an extreme rarity for rocks of any period.

[![Image 5](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/74/Megapnosaurus_.tif/lossy-page1-250px-Megapnosaurus_.tif.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Megapnosaurus_.tif)

_[Grallator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grallator "Grallator")_ footprints made by a trackmaker similar to _[Coelophysis rhodesiensis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coelophysis\_rhodesiensis "Coelophysis rhodesiensis")_, found at the St. George Dinosaur Discovery Site. 

[![Image 6](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4e/Gigandipus.JPG/330px-Gigandipus.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Gigandipus.JPG)

[Gigandipus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gigandipus "Gigandipus") footprint at the site

The **St. George Dinosaur Discovery Site** is a fossil site and museum at Johnson Farm in [Saint George](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_George,_Utah "Saint George, Utah"), [Utah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Utah "Utah").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._George_Dinosaur_Discovery_Site#cite_note-History-1) The museum preserves thousands of dinosaur footprints right at the original site of discovery.

The site was discovered by accident on February 26, 2000 by Dr. Sheldon Johnson, a retired optometrist and resident of St. George. He was in the process of excavating his property when he stumbled upon a large, naturally cut rock. The rock exposed a natural [dinosaur footprint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_footprint "Dinosaur footprint"), which Johnson originally thought to be a complete dinosaur fossil due to the quality of the preservation.

Realizing that these dinosaur tracks would be best served if they were maintained for scientific and educational purposes, Dr. Johnson and his wife, LaVerna, worked to set aside the land and its fossils. Eventually the Johnsons donated the tracks that had been found and arranged for the land to be cared for by the City of St. George. They worked with scientists, local businesses, and government officials on the local, state, and national levels to create the museum which opened in 2005 and is here today. They set up the foundation that continues to preserve the site as a creative learning environment.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._George_Dinosaur_Discovery_Site#cite_note-History-1)

The best preserved and most numerous tracks today form the in-place trackway and exhibits of the St. George Dinosaur Discovery Site. Many other fossils including bones of dinosaurs and fish, shells of small aquatic animals, and leaves and seeds of plants, have joined the footprints, enabling palaeontologists to reconstruct the nearly 200 million-year-old ecosystem preserved here with unprecedented clarity, an extreme rarity for rocks of any period.

**St. George** or **Saint George**[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._George,_Utah#cite_note-gnis-2) is a city in and the [county seat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_seat "County seat") of [Washington County, Utah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_County,_Utah "Washington County, Utah"), United States. It is Utah's [fifth-most populous city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_municipalities_in_Utah "List of municipalities in Utah") and the largest outside the [Wasatch Front](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wasatch_Front "Wasatch Front"), with a population of 95,342 at the [2020 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._George,_Utah#cite_note-2020_Census_(City)-3) The St. George [metropolitan statistical area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_statistical_area "Metropolitan statistical area") has an estimated 208,000 residents. Located in southwestern Utah on the [Arizona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arizona "Arizona")-Utah border, it lies in the northeasternmost part of the [Mojave Desert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mojave_Desert "Mojave Desert"), immediately south of the [Pine Valley Mountains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pine_Valley_Mountains "Pine Valley Mountains"), which mark the southern boundary of the [Great Basin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Basin "Great Basin"). St. George lies slightly northwest of the [Colorado Plateau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Plateau "Colorado Plateau"), which ends at the [Hurricane Fault](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Fault "Hurricane Fault").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._George,_Utah#cite_note-6)

St. George was settled in 1861 to be a cotton mission, earning it the nickname of "[Dixie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Utah's_Dixie "Utah's Dixie")". While the crop never became a successful commodity, the area steadily grew in population. Today, the St. George region is known for its somewhat milder climate compared to the rest of the state, outdoor recreation, which includes [state parks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_park "State park") and [Zion National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zion_National_Park "Zion National Park"). The city has [Utah Tech University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Utah_Tech_University "Utah Tech University"), an [NCAA Division I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NCAA_Division_I "NCAA Division I") institution. St. George is 118 miles (190 km) northeast of [Las Vegas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas "Las Vegas"), [Nevada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nevada "Nevada") and 300 miles (480 km) south-southwest of [Salt Lake City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salt_Lake_City "Salt Lake City") on [Interstate 15](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_15_in_Utah "Interstate 15 in Utah").

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._George,_Utah&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

[![Image 14](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4d/Brigham_Young%27s_winter_home_St_George.jpg/250px-Brigham_Young%27s_winter_home_St_George.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Brigham_Young's_winter_home_St_George.jpg)

[Brigham Young Winter Home and Office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brigham_Young_Winter_Home_and_Office "Brigham Young Winter Home and Office") in St. George

St. George was founded as part of the cotton mission[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._George,_Utah#cite_note-7) in 1861 under the direction of Latter Day Saint [apostle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apostle_(Latter_Day_Saints) "Apostle (Latter Day Saints)")[Erastus Snow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erastus_Snow "Erastus Snow"). At the outbreak of the [American Civil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Civil_War "American Civil War"), [Brigham Young](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brigham_Young "Brigham Young") accelerated the colonization effort:

> Fearing that the war would take away the cotton supply, he began plans for raising enough in this southwestern country to supply the needs of his people. Enough favorable reports had come to him from this warm region below the rim of the Great Basin, that he was convinced cotton could be raised successfully here. At the general church conference in Salt Lake City on October 6th, 1861, about 300 families were "called" to the Dixie mission to promote the cotton industry. Most of the people knew nothing of this expedition until their names were read from the pulpit; but in nearly every case, they responded with good will, and made ready to leave within the month's time allotted to them. The families were selected so as to ensure the communities the right number of farmers, masons, blacksmiths, businessmen, educators, carpenters, as needed.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._George,_Utah#cite_note-8)

The settlement was named after [George A. Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_A._Smith "George A. Smith"), an LDS Church apostle.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._George,_Utah#cite_note-9)

In April 1877, the LDS Church completed the [St. George Utah Temple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._George_Utah_Temple "St. George Utah Temple"). It was the church's third [temple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Temple_(LDS_Church) "Temple (LDS Church)") and is the oldest still in active use.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._George,_Utah#cite_note-10)

The [1992 St. George earthquake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_St._George_earthquake "1992 St. George earthquake") destroyed three houses, as well as above- and below-ground utilities, causing about [US$](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_dollar "United States dollar")1 million in damage.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._George,_Utah#cite_note-desnews_19940515-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._George,_Utah#cite_note-ugs_official_1995_report-12)

St. George was the location of the 1997 [United States Academic Decathlon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Academic_Decathlon "United States Academic Decathlon") national finals.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._George,_Utah#cite_note-13)

In January 2005, a 100-year flood occurred throughout the region, due to prolonged heavy rainfall overflowing both the [Virgin River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virgin_River "Virgin River") and [Santa Clara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Clara_River_(Utah) "Santa Clara River (Utah)") River. One person was killed and 28 homes were destroyed by the Santa Clara River.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._George,_Utah#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._George,_Utah#cite_note-15)

### Nuclear contamination

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._George,_Utah&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Nuclear contamination")]

In the early 1950s, St. George received the brunt of the [fallout](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout "Fallout") of above-ground [nuclear testing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_testing "Nuclear testing") at the Yucca Flats/[Nevada Test Site](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nevada_Test_Site "Nevada Test Site") northwest of Las Vegas. Winds routinely carried the fallout of these tests directly through St. George and southern Utah. Marked increases in the frequency of cancer in the population, including leukemia, lymphoma, thyroid cancer, breast cancer, melanoma, bone cancer, brain tumors, and gastrointestinal tract cancers, were reported from the mid-1950s until the early 1980s.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._George,_Utah#cite_note-jama1984-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._George,_Utah#cite_note-17)

In 1980, _[People](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People\_(magazine) "People (magazine)")_ magazine reported that from about 220 cast and crew who filmed in a 1956 movie, _[The Conqueror](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Conqueror\_(1956\_film)#Cancer\_controversy "The Conqueror (1956 film)")_, on location near St. George, 91 had come down with cancer, and 50 had died from it.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._George,_Utah#cite_note-clar-18) Of these, 46 had died of cancer by 1980. Among the cancer deaths were [John Wayne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Wayne "John Wayne"), [Pedro Armendáriz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pedro_Armend%C3%A1riz "Pedro Armendáriz"), and [Susan Hayward](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susan_Hayward "Susan Hayward"), the film's stars.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._George,_Utah#cite_note-clar-18) But the lifetime odds of developing cancer for men in the U.S. population are 43% and the odds of dying of cancer are 23% (38 and 19%, respectively, for men and women).[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._George,_Utah#cite_note-19) This places the cancer mortality rate for the 220 primary cast and crew quite near the expected average.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._George,_Utah#cite_note-20)

A 1962 [United States Atomic Energy Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Atomic_Energy_Commission "United States Atomic Energy Commission") report found children living in St. George at the time of the fallout may have received doses to their thyroids of [radioiodine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radioiodine "Radioiodine") as high as 120 to 440 rads (1.2 to 4.4 Gy).[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._George,_Utah#cite_note-ieer-21)

According to the [United States Census Bureau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Census_Bureau "United States Census Bureau"), the city has an area of 77.151 square miles (199.82 km 2), of which 0.003 square miles (0.0078 km 2) (0.72% or about 2 ac) is covered by water.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._George,_Utah#cite_note-CenPopGazetteer2023-1) St. George is in a desert valley, with most of the city lying below 3,000 feet (900 m) in elevation. It is near a geological transition zone where the Colorado Plateau and Great Basin converge. The [Beaver Dam Mountains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beaver_Dam_Mountains "Beaver Dam Mountains")/Utah Hill lie to the west, the [Red Cliffs National Conservation Area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Cliffs_National_Conservation_Area "Red Cliffs National Conservation Area") and [Pine Valley Mountains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pine_Valley_Mountains "Pine Valley Mountains") to the north, the western edge of the Colorado Plateau and Zion National Park to the east, and the [Arizona Strip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arizona_Strip "Arizona Strip") to the south. The [Virgin River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virgin_River "Virgin River"), the Santa Clara River, and the seasonal Fort Pearce Wash flow through the St. George valley and converge near the western base of [Webb Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Webb_Hill "Webb Hill") near the city center.

Some roads have names along with numerals, such as "400 East", which is also known as "Flood Street".[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._George,_Utah#cite_note-22)

### Climate

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._George,_Utah&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Climate")]

St. George's arid climate is significantly warmer on average than the rest of the state, and more closely resembles nearby Las Vegas. The climate is cold [arid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desert_climate "Desert climate") (_BWk_), though the average yearly temperature falls around 1°F below the hot arid classification. St. George has long, hot summers and relatively mild winters. The monthly average temperature ranges from 42.1°F (5.6°C) in December to 87.8°F (31.0°C) in July. On average, 60 afternoons have high temperatures over 100°F (38°C), with an average window of June 29 through August 13, and 122 days with high temperatures over 90°F (32°C) with the average window fluctuating between late April and early October. About 60 mornings have low temperature drops to the freezing mark, with the historical average window between November 12 and March 14.

The highest temperature statewide was 118°F (48°C), which was recorded in south St. George, near the Arizona border on July 4, 2007, breaking the previous record holder, at 117°F (47°C), also set in St. George on July 5, 1985.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._George,_Utah#cite_note-NOAA-23) The record high minimum temperature is 89°F (32°C) set on July 15, 1970, and July 3, 2013. Nighttime freezes are common during the winter due to radiational cooling. Both the record low temperature of −11°F (−24°C) and record low maximum temperature of 17°F (−8°C) were set on January 22, 1937; the record low temperature occurred again on January 26, 1937, both during the record cold month of January 1937 across the Western United States.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._George,_Utah#cite_note-NOAA-23)

The city has abundant sunshine year-round and averages about 300 sunny days per year, with an average 8.80 inches (224 mm) of precipitation annually.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._George,_Utah#cite_note-NOAA-23) The wettest "rain year" has been from July 2004 to June 2005 with at least 15.66 inches (398 mm) (some days were missing) and the driest from July 1973 to June 1974 with 3.89 inches (98.8 mm). Record-breaking widespread flooding occurred during January 2005 when area creeks and rivers far exceeded their banks and washed out homes and some neighborhoods. The wettest month has been January 1993, when 4.74 inches (120 mm) fell. Precipitation is fairly evenly distributed throughout the year, except for a markedly drier period from April through June, which occurs after the Pacific storm season ends, but before the southwest monsoon begins, usually in mid-July. Precipitation mostly comes from the Pacific Ocean from late fall through early spring. The storm track usually lifts north of the city by mid-April. The monsoon brings localized and often intense thunderstorms from early July through mid-September. The greatest rainfall in 24 hours was 2.40 inches (61 mm) on August 31, 1909.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._George,_Utah#cite_note-NOAA-23)

The St. George valley occasionally receives wet or slushy snowfall in the winter, but what accumulates usually melts off by the mid- to late morning; the normal seasonal snowfall is 1.4 inches (3.6 cm).[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._George,_Utah#cite_note-NOAA-23) The earliest snowfall was measured on October 29, 1971, and the latest on April 11, 1927.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._George,_Utah#cite_note-NOAA-23) The record single-day snowfall is 10.0 inches (25 cm), which was set on January 5, 1974. With the city having elevations ranging from 2,500 to about 3,500 feet (760 to about 1,070 m), some areas such as Diamond Valley and Winchester Hills typically receive more snowfall and colder temperatures than the rest of the lower valley. The most recent major snow event was on December 8, 2013, when between 6.0 and 8.0 inches (15 and 20 cm) virtually shut down the city, making it the third-heaviest snowfall in the city's history. Also significant about the storm was how low temperatures dropped and remained so for several days with daytime highs failing to reach the freezing mark, and one nighttime low temperature of 1°F (−17°C), recorded at the airport, was the coldest in the city in over 100 years. The cold spell killed or severely damaged much of the area's non-native vegetation, such as the [Mexican fan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washingtonia_filifera_var._robusta "Washingtonia filifera var. robusta") palm trees.

### 2020 census

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._George,_Utah&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: 2020 census")]

As of the [2020 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), St. George had a population of 95,342. The median age was 36.7 years. 25.7% of residents were under the age of 18 and 22.4% of residents were 65 years of age or older. For every 100 women there were 94.7 men, and for every 100 women age 18 and over there were 91.7 men age 18 and over.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._George,_Utah#cite_note-Census2020DP-30)

95.5% of residents lived in urban areas, while 4.5% lived in rural areas.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._George,_Utah#cite_note-Census2020DHC-31)

There were 33,554 households in St. George, of which 31.6% had children under the age of 18 living in them. Of all households, 58.1% were married-couple households, 14.0% were households with a male householder and no spouse or partner present, and 23.5% were households with a female householder and no spouse or partner present. About 21.6% of all households were made up of individuals and 12.6% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._George,_Utah#cite_note-Census2020DP-30)

There were 39,933 housing units, of which 16.0% were vacant. The homeowner vacancy rate was 1.8% and the rental vacancy rate was 8.1%.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._George,_Utah#cite_note-Census2020DP-30)

### 2010 census

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._George,_Utah&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: 2010 census")]

As of the [2010 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_United_States_census "2010 United States census"), 72,897 people, 27,552 households, and 13,042 families resided in the city. The [population density](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_density "Population density") was 1,135 people per square mile. There were 32,089 housing units at an average density of 415.9 per square mile. The city's racial makeup was 87.2% [White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_(U.S._Census) "White (U.S. Census)"), 0.7% [African-American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African-American_(U.S._Census) "African-American (U.S. Census)"), 1.5% [Native American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_American_(U.S._Census) "Native American (U.S. Census)"), 0.8% [Asian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asian_(U.S._Census) "Asian (U.S. Census)"), 1.0% [Pacific Islander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Islander_(U.S._Census) "Pacific Islander (U.S. Census)"), and 8.9% from [other races](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_(United_States_Census) "Race (United States Census)"). 12.8% of the population was [Hispanic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hispanic_(U.S._Census) "Hispanic (U.S. Census)") or [Latino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latino_(U.S._Census) "Latino (U.S. Census)") of any race.

### 2000 census

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._George,_Utah&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: 2000 census")]

As of the [2000 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_United_States_census "2000 United States census"), 49,728 people, 17,367 households, and 13,042 families resided in the city. The [population density](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_density "Population density") was 771.2 people per square mile (297.7/km 2). The 21,083 housing units had an average density of 327.4 per square mile (126.4/km 2). The [racial makeup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_(United_States_Census) "Race (United States Census)") of the city was 92.27% White, 0.24% African American, 1.64% Native American, 0.57% Asian, 0.59% Pacific Islander, 2.87% from other races, and 1.83% from two or more races. Hispanics or Latinos of any race were 6.72% of the population.

Of the 17,367 households, 34.2% had children under 18 living with them, 63.6% were married couples living together, 8.6% had a female householder with no husband present, and 24.9% were not families. About 19.4% of all households were made up of individuals, and 10.2% have someone living alone who was 65 or older. The average household size was 2.81 and the average family size was 3.21.

In the city, the age distribution was 28.4% under 18, 13.7% from 18 to 24, 22.0% from 25 to 44, 16.8% from 45 to 64, and 19.3% who were 65 or older. The median age was 31 years. For every 100 women, there were 94.5 men. For every 100 women 18 and over, there were 91.2 men.

The median income for a household in the city was $36,505, and for a family was $41,788. Men had a median income of $31,106 versus $20,861 for women. The per capita income for the city was $17,022. About 7.4% of families and 11.6% of the population were below the [poverty line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poverty_line "Poverty line"), including 14.4% of those under 18 and 4.4% of those 65 or over.

## Economy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._George,_Utah&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Economy")]

[SkyWest Airlines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SkyWest_Airlines "SkyWest Airlines"), headquartered in St. George, is the primary airline provider at the city's regional airport.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._George,_Utah#cite_note-35)

The [Washington County School District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_County_School_District_(Utah) "Washington County School District (Utah)") main offices are based in the city.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._George,_Utah#cite_note-36)

The [Cafe Rio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cafe_Rio "Cafe Rio") restaurant chain was started in St. George in 1997,[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._George,_Utah#cite_note-37) but is now headquartered in Salt Lake City. The [Swig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swig_(restaurant) "Swig (restaurant)") restaurant chain was founded in St. George.

The local economy is largely based on tourism, manufacturing, and new-home construction.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] Over a dozen golf courses offer year-round golfing, and various world-recognized events also make for large contributors to the city's economy. The city is a popular [retirement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retirement "Retirement") destination[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._George,_Utah#cite_note-38) and also hosts a significant number of vacation homes for people who primarily live in colder areas.

## Sports

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._George,_Utah&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Sports")]

The St. George community has been the home to two minor-league independent baseball teams. The first, the [St. George Pioneerzz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._George_Pioneerzz "St. George Pioneerzz") (originally the Zion Pioneerzz), played in the independent [Western Baseball League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Baseball_League "Western Baseball League") from 1999 to 2001, winning the league championship in 2000. A new franchise, managed by former major league player Darell Evans, was awarded to St. George in 2007. The team, the [St. George Roadrunners](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._George_Roadrunners "St. George Roadrunners"), played in the independent [Golden Baseball League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Baseball_League "Golden Baseball League") before being taken over by the league and moved to [Henderson, Nevada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henderson,_Nevada "Henderson, Nevada"), in 2010.

St. George area high schools—Crimson Cliffs, Dixie, Desert Hills, Pine View, and Snow Canyon—all play in 4A state competition as part of 4A Region 9 with nearby Hurricane High School in [Hurricane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane,_Utah "Hurricane, Utah") and Cedar High School in [Cedar City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cedar_City,_Utah "Cedar City, Utah").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._George,_Utah#cite_note-40)[Utah Tech University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Utah_Tech_University "Utah Tech University") participates in the [NCAA Division I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NCAA_Division_I "NCAA Division I")[Western Athletic Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Athletic_Conference "Western Athletic Conference"). In January 2019, Dixie State announced they were reclassifying to [NCAA Division I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NCAA_Division_I "NCAA Division I") and joining the [Western Athletic Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Athletic_Conference "Western Athletic Conference").[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._George,_Utah#cite_note-41) Former DSU athletes include [Corey Dillon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corey_Dillon "Corey Dillon"), [Anton Palepoi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anton_Palepoi "Anton Palepoi"), [Reno Mahe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reno_Mahe "Reno Mahe"), and [Scott Brumfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_Brumfield "Scott Brumfield"), who all later played in the NFL, and [Marcus Banks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marcus_Banks "Marcus Banks"), [Lionel Hollins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lionel_Hollins "Lionel Hollins"), [Keon Clark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keon_Clark "Keon Clark"), and Mo Baker were Dixie players who later played in the NBA. Utah Tech athletes are called Trailblazers (formerly the Rebels and Red Storm), and former Trailblazers [Bradley Thompson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bradley_Thompson "Bradley Thompson") and [Brandon Lyon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brandon_Lyon "Brandon Lyon") later played in major league baseball, while [Bruce Hurst](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruce_Hurst "Bruce Hurst") of Dixie High School later played for the [Boston Red Sox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston_Red_Sox "Boston Red Sox") as a pitcher, and then ended up managing the now-retired Zion Pioneerzz for its inaugural 1999 season (1999).

St. George has hosted [Ironman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ironman_Triathlon "Ironman Triathlon") and [Ironman 70.3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ironman_70.3 "Ironman 70.3") events, including the 2021 Ironman 70.3 World Championships. In May 2021, the Ironman World Championship hosted by the city due to the COVID-19 and the original venue, Kona, being unable to host. This was the first time that the [Ironman World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ironman_World_Championship "Ironman World Championship") has been hosted outside of Hawai'i.

## Parks and recreation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._George,_Utah&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Parks and recreation")]

The St. George parks division manages over 20 city parks and nearly 60 miles of paved urban trails interlinking neighborhoods, communities, parks, and open space. The city also has over a dozen award-winning golf courses, making the area a Southwestern golfing mecca.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._George,_Utah#cite_note-42) Major parks and sites include the Canyons Softball Complex, Little Valley Softball Complex, Pioneer Park, Tonaquint Nature Center, nationally recognized Snake Hollow bike park, Thunder Junction All Abilities dinosaur theme park, [Red Hills Desert Garden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Hills_Desert_Garden "Red Hills Desert Garden") - a public water-conservation garden displaying both native and exotic flora suited for the local climate, and three local skate parks; Legacy Regional Park and fairgrounds are just east of the city in Hurricane. The St. George area has several public recreation centers, the St. George Rec Center, Washington City Rec Center, and Sand Hollow Aquatics Center.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._George,_Utah#cite_note-43)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._George,_Utah#cite_note-44) St. George is fast becoming a popular rock-climbing and mountain-biking destination.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._George,_Utah#cite_note-45)

## Government

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._George,_Utah&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Government")]

[![Image 20](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/be/Wactyutah5thdist.jpg/250px-Wactyutah5thdist.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Wactyutah5thdist.jpg)

5th District Courthouse

The city of St. George has a council-manager form of government, with five representatives elected [at large](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/At-large "At-large"). The mayor, also elected at large, also serves as a member on the city council. The council hires a city manager to deal with regular operations.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._George,_Utah#cite_note-46)As of January 2021[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._George,_Utah&action=edit), the mayor of St. George is Michele Randall. The city manager is John Willis.

[![Image 21](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/db/Graveyard_In_St._George_Utah_US.jpg/250px-Graveyard_In_St._George_Utah_US.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Graveyard_In_St._George_Utah_US.jpg)

St. George [City Cemetery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cemeteries_in_Utah "List of cemeteries in Utah") (East Tabrnacle at 700 East)

Council members are Jimmy Hughes, Dannielle Larkin, Natalie Larsen, Michelle Tanner, and Steve Kemp. City council meetings are held on the first and third Thursdays of each month at the city council chambers.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._George,_Utah#cite_note-47)

The U.S. Federal Courthouse, Washington County Justice Court, Juvenile Court, and the Fifth District Courthouse are downtown.

#### Television

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._George,_Utah&action=edit&section=27 "Edit section: Television")]

St. George is in the Salt Lake City market, so it has only one television station licensed to the city, [KMYU](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KMYU "KMYU"), a [MyNetworkTV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MyNetworkTV "MyNetworkTV") affiliate on channel 12.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._George,_Utah#cite_note-communitymediadatabase.org-51) KMYU (known as My Utah TV)[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._George,_Utah#cite_note-52) is sister station to [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS") affiliate [KUTV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KUTV "KUTV"), and operates out of KUTV's offices in Salt Lake City, although the station has a news bureau with a reporter and photographer based in St. George and KUTV simulcasts on KMYU-DT2. Also in St. George are the offices of [Cedar City, Utah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cedar_City,_Utah "Cedar City, Utah")–licensed[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._George,_Utah#cite_note-communitymediadatabase.org-51)[KCSG](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KCSG "KCSG") Channel 8, a [MeTV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MeTV "MeTV") owned-and-operated station. The city also receives local TV channels from Salt Lake City with [broadcast translators](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadcast_translators "Broadcast translators") in the St. George area.

[NBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC "NBC")'s Las Vegas affiliate, [KSNV-DT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KSNV-DT "KSNV-DT"), has a local translator owned by Cherry Creek Radio, KVBT-LP channel 41, on which some of its programming airs two hours later than the same programming broadcast on Salt Lake City NBC affiliate [KSL-TV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KSL-TV "KSL-TV").

## Infrastructure

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._George,_Utah&action=edit&section=28 "Edit section: Infrastructure")]

### Healthcare

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._George,_Utah&action=edit&section=29 "Edit section: Healthcare")]

[St. George Regional Hospital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._George_Regional_Hospital "St. George Regional Hospital") is an [Intermountain Health Care](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intermountain_Health_Care "Intermountain Health Care") hospital and the only 24-hour trauma center between Las Vegas and the Wasatch Front, serving the tristate region of southern Utah, northwest Arizona, and southeastern Nevada.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._George,_Utah#cite_note-53)

### Utilities

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._George,_Utah&action=edit&section=30 "Edit section: Utilities")]

St. George is served by City of St. George Power, which serves most of the city, and Dixie Power, which serves southern areas of the city. [Rocky Mountain Power](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocky_Mountain_Power "Rocky Mountain Power") serves parts of the greater St. George area. The municipal water department obtains its own water from wells located near [Gunlock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gunlock,_Utah "Gunlock, Utah") and in [Snow Canyon State Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snow_Canyon_State_Park "Snow Canyon State Park"), Mountain Springs on Pine Valley Mountain. It also purchases wholesale water from the [Washington County Water Conservancy District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_County_Water_Conservancy_District "Washington County Water Conservancy District"), which is sourced from the Virgin River and purified at the Quail Creek Water Treatment Plant.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._George,_Utah#cite_note-54)

St. George Telecommunications, such as Internet, are provided by [TDS Telecom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TDS_Telecom "TDS Telecom") (cable/fiber), [CenturyLink](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lumen_Technologies "Lumen Technologies") (DSL/fiber), [Quantum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lumen_Technologies "Lumen Technologies")(fiber) and [InfoWest](http://infowest.com/) ([WISP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wireless_Internet_service_provider "Wireless Internet service provider")/fiber)

### Transportation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._George,_Utah&action=edit&section=31 "Edit section: Transportation")]

[![Image 22](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/80/St._George%2C_Utah.jpg/250px-St._George%2C_Utah.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:St._George,_Utah.jpg)

Central St. George, looking east with Zion National Park in the distance

[St. George Regional Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._George_Regional_Airport "St. George Regional Airport") is in southeast St. George on Airport Parkway. The airport is served by [American Airlines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Airlines "American Airlines"), [Delta Air Lines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delta_Air_Lines "Delta Air Lines"), and [United Airlines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Airlines "United Airlines"). All flights are operated by [SkyWest Airlines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SkyWest_Airlines "SkyWest Airlines"). As of 2023, two-way flights to Salt Lake City, [Denver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denver,_CO "Denver, CO"), [Phoenix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phoenix,_AZ "Phoenix, AZ"), [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles,CA "Los Angeles,CA") (LAX), and [Dallas–Fort Worth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas,_TX "Dallas, TX") were available.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._George,_Utah#cite_note-sgu1-55)[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._George,_Utah#cite_note-sgu2-56)

#### Local and regional transportation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._George,_Utah&action=edit&section=32 "Edit section: Local and regional transportation")]

[SunTran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SunTran "SunTran"), the local public transit system, operates seven fixed routes serving most areas of St. George, Washington, and Ivins.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._George,_Utah#cite_note-57) Rent-A-Bike and Spin scooters are available for rated use in numerous locations citywide. [Greyhound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greyhound_Lines "Greyhound Lines") serves St. George on its Denver–Las Vegas and Salt Lake City–Las Vegas routes.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._George,_Utah#cite_note-58)[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._George,_Utah#cite_note-59) Greyhound used to connect with [Amtrak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amtrak "Amtrak")'s [California Zephyr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California_Zephyr "California Zephyr") in Salt Lake City at the Salt Lake Central [Intermodal Hub](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salt_Lake_City_Intermodal_Hub "Salt Lake City Intermodal Hub"), but now stops at Salt Lake International Airport instead as a result of its acquisition by FirstGroup.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._George,_Utah#cite_note-60) St. George is also served by the bus company [Tufesa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TUFESA "TUFESA") and the shuttle companies [Salt Lake Express](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salt_Lake_Express "Salt Lake Express") and St. George Shuttle.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._George,_Utah#cite_note-61)[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._George,_Utah#cite_note-62)

#### Major highways

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._George,_Utah&action=edit&section=33 "Edit section: Major highways")]

Two freeways within St. George include [Interstate 15](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_15_in_Utah "Interstate 15 in Utah") which runs northeast–southwest through the city and [SR-7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Utah_State_Route_7 "Utah State Route 7") (Southern Parkway) which runs east–west through the southern periphery of the city. Other highways in St. George include [SR-8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Utah_State_Route_8 "Utah State Route 8") (Sunset Boulevard), [SR-34](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Utah_State_Route_34 "Utah State Route 34") (St. George Boulevard) and [SR-18](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Utah_State_Route_18 "Utah State Route 18") (Bluff Street); the former two run east–west and the latter runs north–south through St. George.
